ko.title: [리테일 101 #15] 소프트웨어가 되어가는 매장 — 그리고 한 페이지로 보는 이번 학기 총정리

segments.src: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.
segments.tr: > 리테일의 향후 10년은 대부분의 소비자가 전혀 보지 못하는 두 가지 힘에 의해 쓰이고 있습니다. 바로 매장을 데이터 시스템으로 전환하는 기술과, 매대 위의 규칙을 조용히 설정하는 정책입니다. 업계가 어디로 향하고 있는지와 함께, 이번 시리즈에서 다룬 모든 내용을 한 페이지로 요약해 드립니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.
segments.tr: 역사상 대부분의 기간 동안 리테일은 어쩌다 보니 기록을 보관하게 된 **물리적** 비즈니스였습니다.

segments.src: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.
segments.tr: 오늘날 리테일은 어쩌다 보니 건물을 가지게 된 **정보** 비즈니스입니다.

segments.src: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.
segments.tr: 이 단 하나의 반전이 앞으로 다가올 거의 모든 트렌드를 설명합니다.

segments.src: Break it into three layers.
segments.tr: 이를 세 가지 레이어로 나누어 보겠습니다.

segments.src: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**
segments.tr: 리테일 테크("retailtech") — 매장이 고도화된 계측 장비가 되다.**

segments.src: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."
segments.tr: 그 양상은 "로봇이 점원을 대체한다"가 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:
segments.tr: 리테일 체인의 모든 단계에 센서와 피드백 루프가 장착되고 있다는 점입니다.

segments.src: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.
segments.tr: - **감지(Sensing):** RFID 태그, 컴퓨터 비전 카메라, 스마트 선반은 "재고가 40개쯤 있는 것 같다"를 "정확히 37개 있고, 그중 3개는 엉뚱한 통로에 있다"로 바꾸어 놓습니다. 의류 분야의 재고 정확도는 역사적으로 100%를 훨씬 밑돌았으며, 이 격차를 좁히는 것은 실질적인 수익으로 이어집니다. 시스템상에서 누락되었다고 판단하는 상품은 판매할 수 없기 때문입니다.

segments.src: - **Deciding:** Machine-learning demand forecasting, automated replenishment, and algorithmic pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.
segments.tr: - **의사결정(Deciding):** 머신러닝 기반의 수요 예측, 자동 발주, 알고리즘 가격 책정 등이 있습니다. 전자가격표시기(ESL)가 중요한 이유는 가격이 매시간 변하기 때문이 아니라(대부분의 체인은 가격을 거의 변경하지 않으며, 지나치게 공격적으로 변경하면 소비자의 반발을 사게 됩니다), *가격을 변경하는 비용*이 거의 제로에 가깝게 떨어지기 때문입니다. 의사결정 비용이 저렴해지면 더 자주 결정을 내리게 됩니다.

segments.src: - **Selling:** Retail media networks — retailers selling ad space on their own sites, apps, and screens using their own purchase data. This is the most important business-model shift of the last decade. Amazon's advertising business alone runs in the tens of billions of dollars a year, and Walmart, Kroger, Target, and even gas-station chains now run their own. Why it matters: ad revenue carries far higher margins than selling groceries, so it can subsidize low prices. The retailer's real product starts to include *access to its shoppers*.
segments.tr: - **판매(Selling):** 리테일 미디어 네트워크(RMN)는 유통업체가 자체 구매 데이터를 활용하여 자사 사이트, 앱, 스크린의 광고 지면을 판매하는 것입니다. 이는 지난 10년간 가장 중요한 비즈니스 모델의 변화입니다. Amazon의 광고 비전만 해도 연간 수백억 달러 규모에 달하며, Walmart, Kroger, Target은 물론 주유소 체인들까지 자체 네트워크를 운영하고 있습니다. 이것이 중요한 이유: 광고 수익은 식료품 판매보다 마진율이 훨씬 높기 때문에 저렴한 상품 가격을 보조할 수 있습니다. 유통업체의 진짜 상품에 *자사 쇼핑객에 대한 접근 권한*이 포함되기 시작하는 것입니다.

segments.src: - **Fulfilling:** Micro-fulfillment, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery. Note the honest part — these are expensive. Fulfilling a $40 online grocery order costs far more than letting a customer walk the aisles and do the picking for free.
segments.tr: - **풀필먼트(Fulfilling):** 마이크로 풀필먼트, 드라이브스루(curbside) 픽업, 당일 배송 등이 있습니다. 솔직히 말해서 이 서비스들은 비용이 많이 듭니다. 40달러짜리 온라인 식료품 주문을 처리하는 비용은 고객이 직접 통로를 걸어 다니며 무료로 물건을 고르게 하는 것보다 훨씬 더 많이 듭니다.

segments.src: Two cautionary notes, because hype is not analysis.
segments.tr: 과장된 광고는 분석이 아니므로, 두 가지 주의할 점이 있습니다.

segments.src: **Self-checkout** expanded fast, then several chains pulled it back or restricted it after shrink and customer-experience problems.
segments.tr: **셀프 계산대**는 빠르게 확장되었으나, 도난(shrink) 및 고객 경험 문제로 인해 여러 체인에서 이를 철수하거나 제한했습니다.

segments.src: **Fully autonomous "just walk out" stores** proved harder and costlier than early demos suggested; Amazon scaled back the format in its larger grocery stores.
segments.tr: **완전 무인 "저스트 워크 아웃(just walk out)" 매장**은 초기 데모에서 보여준 것보다 더 어렵고 비용이 많이 드는 것으로 입증되었습니다. Amazon은 대형 식료품 매장에서 이 포맷을 축소했습니다.

segments.src: The lesson from Lesson #2's *wheel of retailing* still holds: technology changes the cost curve, but it doesn't repeal the economics.
segments.tr: 레슨 #2의 *리테일의 수레바퀴(wheel of retailing)* 이론이 주는 교훈은 여전히 유효합니다. 기술이 비용 곡선을 변화시킬 수는 있지만, 경제학의 법칙을 폐지할 수는 없습니다.

segments.src: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**
segments.tr: 리테일 정책 — 보이지 않는 규칙서.**

segments.src: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:
segments.tr: 유통업체는 법원과 입법부가 설정한 제약 조건 내에서 운영되며, 규칙의 변화는 그 어떤 머천다이징 의사결정보다 더 큰 이익을 움직일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.
segments.tr: - **판매세:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* 판결(2018년)을 통해 주 정부는 타 주에 위치한 온라인 판매자에게 판매세를 징수하도록 요구할 수 있게 되었습니다. 이로 인해 전자상거래가 누리던 구조적인 가격 우위가 하루아침에 사라졌습니다.

segments.src: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.
segments.tr: - **마켓플레이스 책임:** INFORM 소비자법(2023년부터 시행)은 온라인 마켓플레이스가 대량 판매 제3자 판매자의 신원을 확인하도록 의무화하고 있습니다. 이는 조직적 리테일 범죄 및 모조품에 대응하기 위한 조치입니다.

segments.src: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.
segments.tr: - **결제:** 카드 수수료(interchange fee)는 인건비와 임대료 다음으로 유통업체의 가장 큰 지출 항목 중 하나이며, 수년간의 소송과 반복적인 입법 제안의 대상이 되어 왔습니다.

segments.src: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.
segments.tr: - **개인정보 보호:** 캘리포니아의 CCPA/CPRA를 필두로 한 10여 개 이상의 주 법률은 리테일 미디어의 기반이 되는 쇼핑객 데이터를 수집하고 사용하는 방식을 제한합니다.

segments.src: - **Trade:** Tariffs and the treatment of low-value imported parcels (the "de minimis" exemption) have tightened in recent years — a reminder that one customs rule can reshape an entire business model, as it did for ultra-low-price direct-from-overseas apps.
segments.tr: - **무역:** 최근 몇 년 동안 관세 및 소액 수입 화물에 대한 면세 한도("de minimis" 면제) 규정이 강화되었습니다. 이는 해외 직배송 초저가 앱들의 사례처럼, 단 하나의 통관 규칙이 비즈니스 모델 전체를 재편할 수 있음을 상기시켜 줍니다.

segments.src: - **Labor and sustainability:** Minimum wage, scheduling laws, and packaging/extended-producer-responsibility rules all land directly on store P&Ls.
segments.tr: - **노동 및 지속 가능성:** 최저임금, 근무 일정 법안, 포장재 및 생산자책임재활용(EPR) 규정 등은 모두 매장의 손익계산서(P&L)에 직접적인 영향을 미칩니다.

segments.src: What actually stays constant.**
segments.tr: 실제로 변하지 않고 유지되는 것.**

segments.src: Strip away the tech and the same job remains: *get the right assortment, to the right place, at the right price, at an acceptable cost to serve.* Every trend above is a new way to do that old job — or a new constraint on doing it.
segments.tr: 기술을 걷어내도 본질적인 임무는 동일합니다. *적절한 구색을, 적절한 장소에, 적절한 가격으로, 수용 가능한 서비스 비용으로 제공하는 것*입니다. 위의 모든 트렌드는 이 오래된 임무를 수행하는 새로운 방법이거나, 이를 수행하는 데 따르는 새로운 제약 조건입니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상생활 속에서

segments.src: You're at a Target in Columbus, Ohio, buying a $12.99 bottle of laundry detergent.
segments.tr: 여러분은 오하이오주 콜럼버스의 Target 매장에서 12.99달러짜리 세탁 세제 한 병을 사고 있습니다.

segments.src: Trace what just touched that purchase.
segments.tr: 이 구매 과정에 방금 어떤 것들이 관여했는지 추적해 보겠습니다.

segments.src: You searched "detergent" in the app — the top result was a **sponsored placement** paid for by a brand through Target's retail media network.
segments.tr: 앱에서 "세제"를 검색했을 때 가장 먼저 나온 결과는 Target의 리테일 미디어 네트워크를 통해 브랜드가 비용을 지불한 **스폰서 광고(sponsored placement)**였습니다.

segments.src: The app said the item was in Aisle D24 because an **inventory system** thinks that's where it is.
segments.tr: 앱에서는 해당 상품이 D24 통로에 있다고 안내했는데, 이는 **재고 시스템**이 상품의 위치를 그렇게 파악하고 있기 때문입니다.

segments.src: The shelf price came from an **electronic label**, and it matched the app because unified pricing systems are table stakes now.
segments.tr: 선반의 가격표는 **전자가격표시기**에서 표시된 것이며, 통합 가격 시스템이 이제 기본 사양이 되었기 때문에 앱의 가격과 일치했습니다.

segments.src: You paid with a card; roughly 2–3% of that $12.99 left the retailer as an **interchange fee**.
segments.tr: 카드로 결제하자, 12.99달러 중 약 2~3%가 **카드 수수료**로 유통업체에서 빠져나갔습니다.

segments.src: Sales tax was collected — and would have been collected identically if you'd ordered it online from an out-of-state seller, thanks to *Wayfair*.
segments.tr: 판매세가 징수되었습니다. *Wayfair* 판결 덕분에 타 주의 온라인 판매자에게 주문했더라도 동일하게 판매세가 징수되었을 것입니다.

segments.src: When you scanned out at self-checkout, a camera-based system was watching for scan avoidance.
segments.tr: 셀프 계산대에서 바코드를 찍고 나갈 때, 카메라 기반 시스템이 미결제 통과 행위를 감시하고 있었습니다.

segments.src: Overnight, an **automated replenishment algorithm** will decide whether to reorder, and the data from your basket will help price the next brand's ad slot.
segments.tr: 오늘 밤 사이에 **자동 발주 알고리즘**이 재주문 여부를 결정할 것이며, 장바구니 데이터는 다음 브랜드의 광고 슬롯 가격을 책정하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.

segments.src: One bottle of detergent.
segments.tr: 세제 단 한 병을 샀을 뿐입니다.

segments.src: At least six of the technologies and policies above were involved, and you saw exactly none of them.
segments.tr: 위에서 언급한 기술과 정책 중 최소 6가지가 관여했지만, 여러분의 눈에는 단 하나도 보이지 않았습니다.

segments.src: ## The Whole Series in Three Minutes
segments.tr: ## 3분 만에 보는 시리즈 총정리

segments.src: - **#1–3 — Foundations:** Retailing is the last step of the distribution channel, where value is created through *sorting, breaking bulk, holding inventory, and providing service*. Formats (supermarket, warehouse club, specialty, off-price, e-commerce) evolve through the wheel of retailing: enter cheap and bare-bones, add service, drift upmarket, get undercut by the next entrant.
segments.tr: - **#1–3 — 기초:** 리테일은 유통 채널의 마지막 단계로, *분류, 벌크 해체, 재고 보유, 서비스 제공*을 통해 가치를 창출합니다. 포맷(슈퍼마켓, 창고형 할인점, 전문점, 아울렛, 전자상거래)은 리테일의 수레바퀴를 통해 진화합니다. 저렴하고 기본적인 형태로 진입하여 서비스를 추가하고, 고급화되다가, 다음 진입자에게 가격 경쟁력으로 밀리게 됩니다.

segments.src: - **#4–6 — Customer and location:** Shopper decision-making, segmentation, and trade-area analysis. Location is retail's most expensive irreversible decision — you can change a price tomorrow, not a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: - **#4–6 — 고객과 입지:** 쇼핑객의 의사결정, 세분화, 상권 분석을 다룹니다. 입지는 리테일에서 되돌릴 수 없는 가장 비용이 많이 드는 결정입니다. 가격은 내일 당장 바꿀 수 있지만, 15년짜리 임대차 계약은 바꿀 수 없습니다.

segments.src: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Assortment breadth vs. depth, category management, vendor negotiation, and pricing (cost-plus, competitive, psychological, markdown cadence, EDLP vs. high-low).
segments.tr: - **#7–9 — 머천다이징:** 구색의 폭과 깊이, 카테고리 관리, 제조업체 협상, 가격 책정(원가 가산, 경쟁 대응, 심리적 가격, 할인 주기, EDLP vs. 하이-로우)을 다룹니다.

segments.src: - **#10–12 — Operations:** Supply chain and inventory turnover, store layout and visual merchandising, promotion, loyalty, and CRM.
segments.tr: - **#10–12 — 운영:** 공급망과 재고 회전율, 매장 레이아웃 및 비주얼 머천다이징, 프로모션, 로열티, CRM을 다룹니다.

segments.src: - **#13–14 — Measurement and channels:** Retail's core metrics and the shift from multichannel to omnichannel to *unified commerce* — one inventory pool, one customer record, many touchpoints.
segments.tr: - **#13–14 — 측정 및 채널:** 리테일의 핵심 지표와 멀티채널에서 옴니채널을 거쳐 *통합 커머스(unified commerce)*로의 전환을 다룹니다. 이는 하나의 재고 풀, 하나의 고객 기록, 그리고 다양한 접점을 의미합니다.

segments.src: The one formula worth remembering, in plain text:
segments.tr: 기억해 둘 만한 단 하나의 공식은 다음과 같습니다.

segments.src: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost
segments.tr: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost

segments.src: It's the discipline of the whole field in one line: retail profit comes from **margin × velocity**, not margin alone.
segments.tr: 이 한 줄에 리테일 분야 전체의 규율이 담겨 있습니다. 리테일의 이익은 마진 단독이 아니라 **마진 × 회전율**에서 나옵니다.

segments.src: A high-margin item that never sells loses to a thin-margin item that turns twelve times a year.
segments.tr: 전혀 팔리지 않는 고마진 상품은 일 년에 12번 회전하는 저마진 상품에 패배합니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Retail's frontier is instrumentation — sensing, deciding, selling, and fulfilling are all becoming data loops, with retail media networks the single biggest business-model change.
segments.tr: 1. 리테일의 최전선은 계측화입니다. 감지, 의사결정, 판매, 풀필먼트가 모두 데이터 루프가 되고 있으며, 리테일 미디어 네트워크가 단일 비즈니스 모델 변화 중 가장 큰 축을 담당합니다.

segments.src: 2. Policy is not background noise: sales tax nexus, marketplace verification, interchange fees, privacy law, and trade rules each move real money.
segments.tr: 2. 정책은 배경 소음이 아닙니다. 판매세 징수 기준(nexus), 마켓플레이스 판매자 확인, 카드 수수료, 개인정보 보호법, 무역 규정 등은 각각 실질적인 자금을 움직입니다.

segments.src: 3. Underneath it all, the job hasn't changed — right assortment, right place, right price, acceptable cost to serve — and GMROI is still how you know you're doing it.
segments.tr: 3. 이 모든 것의 밑바탕에서 임무는 변하지 않았습니다. 적절한 구색, 적절한 장소, 적절한 가격, 수용 가능한 서비스 비용이 그것이며, GMROI는 여전히 여러분이 이를 잘 수행하고 있는지 확인하는 핵심 지표입니다.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Retail media network** — A retailer's own advertising business, selling placements on its site, app, and in-store screens using its first-party purchase data.
segments.tr: - **리테일 미디어 네트워크(Retail media network)** — 유통업체의 자체 광고 비즈니스로, 자사의 1차 구매 데이터를 활용하여 사이트, 앱, 매장 내 스크린의 광고 지면을 판매하는 것입니다.

segments.src: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — A digital price display on the shelf edge, updated centrally; its value is driving the cost of a price change toward zero.
segments.tr: - **전자가격표시기(ESL)** — 선반 가장자리에 부착되어 중앙에서 업데이트되는 디지털 가격 표시 장치로, 가격 변경 비용을 거의 제로로 만드는 데 가치가 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Unified commerce** — A single shared inventory, pricing, and customer record behind every channel, as opposed to separate online and store systems stitched together.
segments.tr: - **통합 커머스(Unified commerce)** — 별개의 온라인 및 매장 시스템을 임시로 꿰맞춘 것과 달리, 모든 채널의 이면에 단일한 공유 재고, 가격, 고객 기록을 두는 방식입니다.

segments.src: - **Economic nexus** — The rule, established for sales tax by *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, that a seller can owe tax collection duties in a state based on sales volume there, without a physical location.
segments.tr: - **경제적 넥서스(Economic nexus)** — *South Dakota v. Wayfair* 판결을 통해 판매세 분야에 확립된 규칙으로, 물리적 매장이 없더라도 특정 주에서의 매출 규모를 기준으로 해당 주에서 세금 징수 의무가 발생할 수 있다는 원칙입니다.

segments.src: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Gross margin dollars per dollar of inventory carried; retail's core test of whether margin and turnover are working together.
segments.tr: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment, 재고투자대비 매출총이익률)** — 보유한 재고 1달러당 창출된 매출총이익 달러화 수치로, 마진과 회전율이 유기적으로 잘 작동하고 있는지 평가하는 리테일의 핵심 테스트입니다.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** A retail media network is the retailer monetizing its own audience and purchase data; the high margins on that ad revenue can subsidize lower shelf prices.
segments.tr: *정답: **Q1 — B.** 리테일 미디어 네트워크는 유통업체가 자체 고객층과 구매 데이터를 수익화하는 것입니다. 해당 광고 수익의 높은 마진을 통해 더 저렴한 상품 가격을 보조할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** Frequent demand-based price hikes invite consumer and political backlash, and most chains avoid them.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (거짓).** 수요에 기반한 빈번한 가격 인상은 소비자와 정치권의 반발을 불러일으키기 때문에 대부분의 체인은 이를 피합니다.

segments.src: The real value is operational: near-zero cost per price change, plus shelf-to-app price consistency and less labor spent on paper tags.
segments.tr: 진짜 가치는 운영 측면에 있습니다. 가격 변경당 비용이 거의 제로에 가깝고, 매장과 앱 간의 가격 일관성을 유지할 수 있으며, 종이 가격표 교체에 드는 인건비를 줄일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: **Q3 — C.** Before Wayfair, many remote online sellers weren't required to collect state sales tax, effectively making their prices several percent cheaper than a local store's.
segments.tr: **Q3 — C.** Wayfair 판결 이전에는 많은 원격 온라인 판매자가 주 판매세를 징수할 의무가 없었기 때문에, 결과적으로 지역 매장보다 가격이 몇 퍼센트 더 저렴했습니다.

segments.src: The 2018 decision ended that gap.
segments.tr: 2018년의 이 판결로 그러한 격차가 해소되었습니다.

segments.src: (The INFORM Act targets marketplace seller verification; the CCPA governs data privacy.)*
segments.tr: (INFORM 법안은 마켓플레이스 판매자 신원 확인을 목표로 하며, CCPA는 데이터 개인정보 보호를 규율합니다.)*

zh.title: [零售 101 #15] 实体店正逐渐沦为软件——以及一页纸带你复习整个学期

segments.src: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.
segments.tr: > 零售业的下一个十年正由两股大多数消费者从未察觉的力量书写——将商店变成数据系统的技术，以及默默设定货架规则的政策。以下是行业的发展方向，外加本系列所涵盖内容的单页总结。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.
segments.tr: 在其历史的大部分时间里，零售业是一项顺便保留记录的**实体**业务。

segments.src: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.
segments.tr: 如今，它是一项碰巧拥有建筑物的**信息**业务。

segments.src: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.
segments.tr: 这单一的倒置解释了地平线上的几乎每一个趋势。

segments.src: Break it into three layers.
segments.tr: 将其分解为三个层面。

segments.src: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**
segments.tr: 零售科技（"retailtech"）——商店实现仪器化。**

segments.src: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."
segments.tr: 这种模式不是“机器人取代店员”。

segments.src: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:
segments.tr: 而是零售链中的每一个步骤都在配备传感器和反馈回路：

segments.src: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.
segments.tr: - **感知：** RFID标签、计算机视觉摄像头和智能货架将“我们认为我们有40件”变成“我们知道我们有37件，其中3件在错误的过道里”。服装库存的准确率历史上一直远低于100%，弥补这一差距具有真正的金钱价值——系统认为丢失的东西你是卖不出去的。

segments.src: - **Deciding:** Machine-learning demand forecasting, automated replenishment, and algorithmic pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.
segments.tr: - **决策：** 机器学习需求预测、自动补货和算法定价。电子货架标签（ESLs）在这里很重要，不是因为价格每小时都在变（大多数连锁店很少改变价格，积极这样做会招致强烈的反对），而是因为*更改价格的成本*降到了接近于零。当决策变便宜时，你就会更频繁地做决策。

segments.src: - **Selling:** Retail media networks — retailers selling ad space on their own sites, apps, and screens using their own purchase data. This is the most important business-model shift of the last decade. Amazon's advertising business alone runs in the tens of billions of dollars a year, and Walmart, Kroger, Target, and even gas-station chains now run their own. Why it matters: ad revenue carries far higher margins than selling groceries, so it can subsidize low prices. The retailer's real product starts to include *access to its shoppers*.
segments.tr: - **销售：** 零售媒体网络——零售商利用自己的购买数据，在其自己的网站、应用程序和屏幕上出售广告空间。这是过去十年中最重要的商业模式转变。亚马逊仅广告业务一年的收入就达数百亿美元，而沃尔玛、克罗格、塔吉特甚至加油站连锁店现在也都在运营自己的广告业务。为什么这很重要：广告收入的利润率远高于销售杂货，因此它可以补贴低价。零售商真正的产品开始包括*接触其购物者的权限*。

segments.src: - **Fulfilling:** Micro-fulfillment, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery. Note the honest part — these are expensive. Fulfilling a $40 online grocery order costs far more than letting a customer walk the aisles and do the picking for free.
segments.tr: - **履约：** 微型履约、路边取货和当日达。注意诚实的部分——这些都很昂贵。履约一份40美元的在线杂货订单，成本远高于让顾客自己走过货道并免费挑选。

segments.src: Two cautionary notes, because hype is not analysis.
segments.tr: 两条警示，因为炒作不是分析。

segments.src: **Self-checkout** expanded fast, then several chains pulled it back or restricted it after shrink and customer-experience problems.
segments.tr: **自助结账**迅速扩张，但在出现商品损耗和客户体验问题后，几家连锁店又将其撤回或进行了限制。

segments.src: **Fully autonomous "just walk out" stores** proved harder and costlier than early demos suggested; Amazon scaled back the format in its larger grocery stores.
segments.tr: **完全自主的“即拿即走”商店**证明比早期演示更加困难且成本更高；亚马逊在其较大的杂货店中缩减了该模式。

segments.src: The lesson from Lesson #2's *wheel of retailing* still holds: technology changes the cost curve, but it doesn't repeal the economics.
segments.tr: 来自第2课的*零售轮*的教训依然适用：技术改变了成本曲线，但它并没有废除经济学。

segments.src: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**
segments.tr: 零售政策——无形的规则手册。**

segments.src: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:
segments.tr: 零售商在法院和立法机构设定的约束下运营，规则的改变可以比任何商品化决策带来更多的利润：

segments.src: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.
segments.tr: - **销售税：** *South Dakota v. Wayfair*（2018年）允许各州要求州外在线卖家征收销售税。它一夜之间结束了电子商务的结构性价格优势。

segments.src: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.
segments.tr: - **市场问责制：** 《INFORM消费者法案》（自2023年起生效）要求在线市场验证高容量第三方卖家——这是对有组织的零售犯罪和假冒商品的反应。

segments.src: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.
segments.tr: - **支付：** 银行卡交换（“刷卡”）费用是零售商仅次于劳动力和租金的最大单项支出之一，它们一直是多年诉讼和反复立法提案的主题。

segments.src: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.
segments.tr: - **隐私：** 以加州CCPA/CPRA为首的州法律，加上十几个其他法律，限制了零售媒体背后的购物者数据的收集和使用方式。

segments.src: - **Trade:** Tariffs and the treatment of low-value imported parcels (the "de minimis" exemption) have tightened in recent years — a reminder that one customs rule can reshape an entire business model, as it did for ultra-low-price direct-from-overseas apps.
segments.tr: - **贸易：** 关税和低价值进口包裹的处理（“微量豁免”）近年来收紧了——这提醒我们，一项海关规则可以重塑整个商业模式，正如它对超低价直接海外应用程序所做的那样。

segments.src: - **Labor and sustainability:** Minimum wage, scheduling laws, and packaging/extended-producer-responsibility rules all land directly on store P&Ls.
segments.tr: - **劳动力和可持续性：** 最低工资、排班法和包装/生产者责任延伸规则都直接落在了商店的损益表上。

segments.src: What actually stays constant.**
segments.tr: 什么实际上保持不变。**

segments.src: Strip away the tech and the same job remains: *get the right assortment, to the right place, at the right price, at an acceptable cost to serve.* Every trend above is a new way to do that old job — or a new constraint on doing it.
segments.tr: 剥离技术，同样的工作依然存在：*以可接受的服务成本，将正确的分类、在正确的地点、以正确的价格提供给客户。* 上述每一项趋势都是完成这一旧工作的新方式——或者是完成该工作的新限制。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: You're at a Target in Columbus, Ohio, buying a $12.99 bottle of laundry detergent.
segments.tr: 你在俄亥俄州哥伦布市的一家Target购买一瓶12.99美元的洗衣液。

segments.src: Trace what just touched that purchase.
segments.tr: 追踪刚刚触及该购买的行为。

segments.src: You searched "detergent" in the app — the top result was a **sponsored placement** paid for by a brand through Target's retail media network.
segments.tr: 你在应用程序中搜索了“洗衣液”——最上面的结果是由品牌通过Target的零售媒体网络支付的**赞助展示位置**。

segments.src: The app said the item was in Aisle D24 because an **inventory system** thinks that's where it is.
segments.tr: 该应用程序显示该物品在Aisle D24，因为**库存系统**认为它在那里。

segments.src: The shelf price came from an **electronic label**, and it matched the app because unified pricing systems are table stakes now.
segments.tr: 货架价格来自**电子标签**，它与应用程序相匹配，因为统一的定价系统现在是基本筹码。

segments.src: You paid with a card; roughly 2–3% of that $12.99 left the retailer as an **interchange fee**.
segments.tr: 你用卡付款；这12.99美元中大约2%到3%作为**交换费**离开零售商。

segments.src: Sales tax was collected — and would have been collected identically if you'd ordered it online from an out-of-state seller, thanks to *Wayfair*.
segments.tr: 征收了销售税——如果你从州外卖家那里在线订购，由于*Wayfair*，它也会被同样地征收。

segments.src: When you scanned out at self-checkout, a camera-based system was watching for scan avoidance.
segments.tr: 当你在自助结账处扫描时，基于摄像头的系统正在监视逃避扫描的行为。

segments.src: Overnight, an **automated replenishment algorithm** will decide whether to reorder, and the data from your basket will help price the next brand's ad slot.
segments.tr: 一夜之间，**自动补货算法**将决定是否重新订购，你购物车中的数据将有助于为下一个品牌的广告位定价。

segments.src: One bottle of detergent.
segments.tr: 一瓶洗衣液。

segments.src: At least six of the technologies and policies above were involved, and you saw exactly none of them.
segments.tr: 上述技术和政策中至少有六种参与其中，而你根本没有看到其中任何一种。

segments.src: ## The Whole Series in Three Minutes
segments.tr: ## 三分钟看懂整个系列

segments.src: - **#1–3 — Foundations:** Retailing is the last step of the distribution channel, where value is created through *sorting, breaking bulk, holding inventory, and providing service*. Formats (supermarket, warehouse club, specialty, off-price, e-commerce) evolve through the wheel of retailing: enter cheap and bare-bones, add service, drift upmarket, get undercut by the next entrant.
segments.tr: - **#1–3 — 基础：** 零售是分销渠道的最后一步，价值通过*分类、拆零、持有库存和提供服务*创造。业态（超市、仓储会员店、专业店、折扣店、电子商务）通过零售轮演变：低价和简陋切入，增加服务，向高端漂移，被下一个进入者削弱。

segments.src: - **#4–6 — Customer and location:** Shopper decision-making, segmentation, and trade-area analysis. Location is retail's most expensive irreversible decision — you can change a price tomorrow, not a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: - **#4–6 — 客户与位置：** 购物者决策、细分和贸易区分析。位置是零售最昂贵的不可逆决策——你可以明天改变价格，而不是15年的租约。

segments.src: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Assortment breadth vs. depth, category management, vendor negotiation, and pricing (cost-plus, competitive, psychological, markdown cadence, EDLP vs. high-low).
segments.tr: - **#7–9 — 商品化：** 品类广度与深度、品类管理、供应商谈判和定价（成本加成、竞争性、心理性、降价节奏、EDLP对高低价）。

segments.src: - **#10–12 — Operations:** Supply chain and inventory turnover, store layout and visual merchandising, promotion, loyalty, and CRM.
segments.tr: - **#10–12 — 运营：** 供应链和库存周转、店面布局和视觉陈列、促销、忠诚度和CRM。

segments.src: - **#13–14 — Measurement and channels:** Retail's core metrics and the shift from multichannel to omnichannel to *unified commerce* — one inventory pool, one customer record, many touchpoints.
segments.tr: - **#13–14 — 衡量与渠道：** 零售的核心指标以及从多渠道到全渠道再到*统一商业*的转变——一个库存池、一个客户记录、多个接触点。

segments.src: The one formula worth remembering, in plain text:
segments.tr: 值得记住的一个公式，用纯文本表示：

segments.src: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost
segments.tr: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost

segments.src: It's the discipline of the whole field in one line: retail profit comes from **margin × velocity**, not margin alone.
segments.tr: 这是整个领域的纪律，只有一行：零售利润来自**利润率×周转率**，而不是单单利润率。

segments.src: A high-margin item that never sells loses to a thin-margin item that turns twelve times a year.
segments.tr: 从不畅销的高利润率商品输给了一年周转十二次的薄利多销商品。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Retail's frontier is instrumentation — sensing, deciding, selling, and fulfilling are all becoming data loops, with retail media networks the single biggest business-model change.
segments.tr: 1. 零售的前沿是仪器化——感知、决策、销售和履约都在变成数据循环，零售媒体网络是单一最大的商业模式变革。

segments.src: 2. Policy is not background noise: sales tax nexus, marketplace verification, interchange fees, privacy law, and trade rules each move real money.
segments.tr: 2. 政策不是背景噪音：销售税连接点、市场验证、交换费、隐私法和贸易规则各自牵动着真金白银。

segments.src: 3. Underneath it all, the job hasn't changed — right assortment, right place, right price, acceptable cost to serve — and GMROI is still how you know you're doing it.
segments.tr: 3. 在这一切之下，工作并没有改变——正确的分类、正确的地点、正确的价格、可接受的服务成本——而GMROI仍然是你如何知道你在做这件事的方式。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Retail media network** — A retailer's own advertising business, selling placements on its site, app, and in-store screens using its first-party purchase data.
segments.tr: - **Retail media network** — 零售商自己的广告业务，利用其第一方购买数据在其网站、应用程序和店内屏幕上销售展示位置。

segments.src: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — A digital price display on the shelf edge, updated centrally; its value is driving the cost of a price change toward zero.
segments.tr: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — 货架边缘的数字价格显示器，集中更新；其价值在于将价格更改的成本推向零。

segments.src: - **Unified commerce** — A single shared inventory, pricing, and customer record behind every channel, as opposed to separate online and store systems stitched together.
segments.tr: - **Unified commerce** — 每个渠道背后都有一个单一的共享库存、定价和客户记录，而不是拼凑在一起的独立在线和店面系统。

segments.src: - **Economic nexus** — The rule, established for sales tax by *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, that a seller can owe tax collection duties in a state based on sales volume there, without a physical location.
segments.tr: - **Economic nexus** — 针对销售税由*South Dakota v. Wayfair*确立的规则，即卖家可以根据那里的销售量在一个州承担纳税征收职责，而无需实体位置。

segments.src: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Gross margin dollars per dollar of inventory carried; retail's core test of whether margin and turnover are working together.
segments.tr: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — 每持有一美元库存的毛利美元；零售商检验利润率和周转率是否协同工作的核心测试。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** A retail media network is the retailer monetizing its own audience and purchase data; the high margins on that ad revenue can subsidize lower shelf prices.
segments.tr: *答案：**Q1 — B。** 零售媒体网络是零售商将其自己的受众和购买数据货币化；该广告收入的高利润率可以补贴较低的货架价格。

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** Frequent demand-based price hikes invite consumer and political backlash, and most chains avoid them.

segments.src: The real value is operational: near-zero cost per price change, plus shelf-to-app price consistency and less labor spent on paper tags.
segments.tr: 真正的价值是运营性的：每个价格更改的成本接近于零，加上货架到应用程序的价格一致性以及在纸质标签上花费的劳动力减少。

segments.src: **Q3 — C.** Before Wayfair, many remote online sellers weren't required to collect state sales tax, effectively making their prices several percent cheaper than a local store's.
segments.tr: **Q3 — C。** 在Wayfair之前，许多远程在线卖家不需要征收州销售税，实际上使他们的价格比本地商店便宜几个百分点。

hi.title: [Retailing 101 #15] The Store Is Becoming Software — and Your Whole Semester on One Page

segments.src: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.
segments.tr: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Today's Concept

segments.src: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.
segments.tr: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.

segments.src: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.
segments.tr: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.

segments.src: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.
segments.tr: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.

segments.src: Break it into three layers.
segments.tr: Break it into three layers.

segments.src: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**
segments.tr: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**

segments.src: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."
segments.tr: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."

segments.src: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:
segments.tr: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:

segments.src: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.
segments.tr: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.

segments.src: - **Deciding:** Machine-learning demand forecasting, automated replenishment, and algorithmic pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.

Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.

segments.src: - **Selling:** Retail media networks — retailers selling ad space on their own sites, apps, and screens using their own purchase data. This is the most important business-model shift of the last decade. Amazon's advertising business alone runs in the tens of billions of dollars a year, and Walmart, Kroger, Target, and even gas-station chains now run their own. Why it matters: ad revenue carries far higher margins than selling groceries, so it can subsidize low prices. The retailer's real product starts to include *access to its shoppers*.

segments.src: - **Fulfilling:** Micro-fulfillment, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery. Note the honest part — these are expensive. Fulfilling a $40 online grocery order costs far more than letting a customer walk the aisles and do the picking for free.

segments.src: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**
segments.tr: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**

segments.src: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:
segments.tr: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:

segments.src: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.
segments.tr: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.

segments.src: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.
segments.tr: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.

segments.src: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.
segments.tr: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.

segments.src: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.
segments.tr: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.

segments.src: - **Trade:** Tariffs and the treatment of low-value imported parcels (the "de minimis" exemption) have tightened in recent years — a reminder that one customs rule can reshape an entire business model, as it did for ultra-low-price direct-from-overseas apps.

segments.src: - **Labor and sustainability:** Minimum wage, scheduling laws, and packaging/extended-producer-responsibility rules all land directly on store P&Ls.

segments.tr: What actually stays constant.**

es.title: [Retailing 101 #15] La tienda se está convirtiendo en software y todo tu semestre en una sola página

segments.src: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.
segments.tr: > La próxima década del comercio minorista está siendo escrita por dos fuerzas que la mayoría de los compradores nunca ven: la tecnología que convierte la tienda en un sistema de datos y la política que establece silenciosamente las reglas de los estantes. Aquí es hacia dónde se dirige la industria, además de un resumen de una página de todo lo que cubrió esta serie.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El concepto de hoy

segments.src: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.
segments.tr: Durante la mayor parte de su historia, el comercio minorista fue un negocio **físico** que casualmente llevaba registros.

segments.src: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.
segments.tr: Hoy en día es un negocio de **información** que casualmente tiene edificios.

segments.src: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.
segments.tr: Esa única inversión explica casi todas las tendencias en el horizonte.

segments.src: Break it into three layers.
segments.tr: Divídelo en tres capas.

segments.src: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**
segments.tr: Tecnología minorista ("retailtech"): la tienda se instrumenta.**

segments.src: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."
segments.tr: El patrón no es "los robots reemplazan a los dependientes".

segments.src: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:
segments.tr: Es que cada paso en la cadena minorista está recibiendo un sensor y un bucle de retroalimentación:

segments.src: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.
segments.tr: - **Detección:** Las etiquetas RFID, las cámaras de visión artificial y los estantes inteligentes convierten "creemos que tenemos 40 unidades" en "sabemos que tenemos 37, y 3 están en el pasillo equivocado". La precisión del inventario en indumentaria ha rondado históricamente muy por debajo del 100%, y cerrar esa brecha vale dinero real; no puedes vender lo que tu sistema cree que falta.

segments.src: - **Deciding:** Machine-learning demand forecasting, automated replenishment, and algorithmic pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.
segments.tr: - **Decisión:** Pronóstico de demanda por aprendizaje automático, reabastecimiento automatizado y precios algorítmicos. Las etiquetas electrónicas de estantes (ESL) importan aquí no porque los precios cambien cada hora (la mayoría de las cadenas los cambian raramente, y hacerlo agresivamente invita a reacciones negativas), sino porque el *costo de cambiar un precio* cae casi a cero. Cuando una decisión se vuelve barata, la tomas más a menudo.

segments.src: - **Selling:** Retail media networks — retailers selling ad space on their own sites, apps, and screens using their own purchase data. This is the most important business-model shift of the last decade. Amazon's advertising business alone runs in the tens of billions of dollars a year, and Walmart, Kroger, Target, and even gas-station chains now run their own. Why it matters: ad revenue carries far higher margins than selling groceries, so it can subsidize low prices. The retailer's real product starts to include *access to its shoppers*.
segments.tr: - **Venta:** Redes de medios minoristas: minoristas que venden espacio publicitario en sus propios sitios, aplicaciones y pantallas utilizando sus propios datos de compra. Este es el cambio de modelo de negocio más importante de la última década. El negocio publicitario de Amazon por sí solo asciende a decenas de miles de millones de dólares al año, y Walmart, Kroger, Target y hasta cadenas de gasolineras ahora operan el suyo. Por qué importa: los ingresos por publicidad conllevan márgenes mucho más altos que la venta de comestibles, por lo que pueden subsidiar precios bajos. El producto real del minorista comienza a incluir el *acceso a sus compradores*.

segments.src: - **Fulfilling:** Micro-fulfillment, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery. Note the honest part — these are expensive. Fulfilling a $40 online grocery order costs far more than letting a customer walk the aisles and do the picking for free.
segments.tr: - **Cumplimiento:** Microcumplimiento, recogida en la acera y entrega el mismo día. Nota la parte honesta: estos son caros. Cumplir con un pedido de comestibles en línea de $40 cuesta mucho más que dejar que un cliente camine por los pasillos y haga la selección gratis.

segments.src: Two cautionary notes, because hype is not analysis.
segments.tr: Dos notas de precaución, porque el bombo publicitario no es análisis.

segments.src: **Self-checkout** expanded fast, then several chains pulled it back or restricted it after shrink and customer-experience problems.
segments.tr: **El autopago** se expandió rápidamente, luego varias cadenas lo retiraron o restringieron después de problemas de merma y experiencia del cliente.

segments.src: **Fully autonomous "just walk out" stores** proved harder and costlier than early demos suggested; Amazon scaled back the format in its larger grocery stores.
segments.tr: **Las tiendas totalmente autónomas "just walk out"** demostraron ser más difíciles y costosas de lo que sugerían las primeras demostraciones; Amazon redujo el formato en sus tiendas de comestibles más grandes.

segments.src: The lesson from Lesson #2's *wheel of retailing* still holds: technology changes the cost curve, but it doesn't repeal the economics.
segments.tr: La lección de la lección #2 sobre la *rueda del comercio minorista* sigue siendo válida: la tecnología cambia la curva de costos, pero no deroga la economía.

segments.src: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**
segments.tr: Política minorista: el libro de reglas invisible.**

segments.src: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:
segments.tr: Los minoristas operan dentro de restricciones establecidas por los tribunales y las legislaturas, y un cambio de regla puede mover más ganancias que cualquier decisión de comercialización:

segments.src: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.
segments.tr: - **Impuesto sobre las ventas:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) permitió a los estados exigir a los vendedores en línea de fuera del estado que recauden el impuesto sobre las ventas. Puso fin a una ventaja de precios estructural para el comercio electrónico de la noche a la mañana.

segments.src: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.
segments.tr: - **Responsabilidad del mercado:** La Ley INFORM Consumers (en vigor desde 2023) exige que los mercados en línea verifiquen a los vendedores de terceros de gran volumen, una respuesta al crimen minorista organizado y a los productos falsificados.

segments.src: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.
segments.tr: - **Pagos:** Las tarifas de intercambio de tarjetas ("swipe fees") son una de las partidas más grandes de un minorista después de la mano de obra y el alquiler, y han sido objeto de años de litigios y repetidas propuestas legislativas.

segments.src: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.
segments.tr: - **Privacidad:** Las leyes estatales lideradas por la CCPA/CPRA de California, además de más de una docena de otras, limitan cómo se pueden recopilar y utilizar los datos de los compradores detrás de los medios minoristas.

segments.src: - **Trade:** Tariffs and the treatment of low-value imported parcels (the "de minimis" exemption) have tightened in recent years — a reminder that one customs rule can reshape an entire business model, as it did for ultra-low-price direct-from-overseas apps.
segments.tr: - **Comercio:** Los aranceles y el tratamiento de los paquetes importados de bajo valor (la exención de "de minimis") se han endurecido en los últimos años, un recordatorio de que una regla aduanera puede remodelar todo un modelo de negocio, como lo hizo para las aplicaciones de ultra bajo precio directas desde el extranjero.

segments.src: - **Labor and sustainability:** Minimum wage, scheduling laws, and packaging/extended-producer-responsibility rules all land directly on store P&Ls.
segments.tr: - **Trabajo y sostenibilidad:** El salario mínimo, las leyes de horarios y las reglas de empaquetado y responsabilidad extendida del productor aterrizan directamente en las cuentas de pérdidas y ganancias de las tiendas.

segments.src: What actually stays constant.**
segments.tr: Lo que realmente permanece constante.**

segments.src: Strip away the tech and the same job remains: *get the right assortment, to the right place, at the right price, at an acceptable cost to serve.* Every trend above is a new way to do that old job — or a new constraint on doing it.
segments.tr: Elimina la tecnología y queda el mismo trabajo: *conseguir el surtido correcto, en el lugar correcto, al precio correcto, a un costo aceptable para servir.* Cada tendencia anterior es una nueva forma de hacer ese viejo trabajo, o una nueva restricción para hacerlo.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: You're at a Target in Columbus, Ohio, buying a $12.99 bottle of laundry detergent.
segments.tr: Estás en un Target en Columbus, Ohio, comprando una botella de detergente para ropa de $12.99.

segments.src: Trace what just touched that purchase.
segments.tr: Rastrea lo que acaba de tocar esa compra.

segments.src: You searched "detergent" in the app — the top result was a **sponsored placement** paid for by a brand through Target's retail media network.
segments.tr: Buscaste "detergente" en la aplicación; el resultado principal fue una **colocación patrocinada** pagada por una marca a través de la red de medios minoristas de Target.

segments.src: The app said the item was in Aisle D24 because an **inventory system** thinks that's where it is.
segments.tr: La aplicación decía que el artículo estaba en el pasillo D24 porque un **sistema de inventario** piensa que está ahí.

segments.src: The shelf price came from an **electronic label**, and it matched the app because unified pricing systems are table stakes now.
segments.tr: El precio del estante provenía de una **etiqueta electrónica**, y coincidía con la aplicación porque los sistemas de precios unificados son requisitos indispensables hoy en día.

segments.src: You paid with a card; roughly 2–3% of that $12.99 left the retailer as an **interchange fee**.
segments.tr: Pagaste con tarjeta; aproximadamente del 2 al 3% de esos $12.99 salieron del minorista como una **tarifa de intercambio**.

segments.src: Sales tax was collected — and would have been collected identically if you'd ordered it online from an out-of-state seller, thanks to *Wayfair*.
segments.tr: Se recaudó el impuesto sobre las ventas, y se habría recaudado de manera idéntica si lo hubieras pedido en línea a un vendedor de fuera del estado, gracias a *Wayfair*.

segments.src: When you scanned out at self-checkout, a camera-based system was watching for scan avoidance.
segments.tr: Cuando saliste escaneando en el autopago, un sistema basado en cámaras vigilaba la evasión de escaneo.

segments.src: Overnight, an **automated replenishment algorithm** will decide whether to reorder, and the data from your basket will help price the next brand's ad slot.
segments.tr: Durante la noche, un **algoritmo de reabastecimiento automatizado** decidirá si debe reordenar, y los datos de tu cesta ayudarán a fijar el precio del espacio publicitario de la próxima marca.

segments.src: One bottle of detergent.
segments.tr: Una botella de detergente.

segments.src: At least six of the technologies and policies above were involved, and you saw exactly none of them.
segments.tr: Al menos seis de las tecnologías y políticas anteriores estuvieron involucradas, y no viste absolutamente ninguna de ellas.

segments.src: ## The Whole Series in Three Minutes
segments.tr: ## Toda la serie en tres minutos

segments.src: - **#1–3 — Foundations:** Retailing is the last step of the distribution channel, where value is created through *sorting, breaking bulk, holding inventory, and providing service*. Formats (supermarket, warehouse club, specialty, off-price, e-commerce) evolve through the wheel of retailing: enter cheap and bare-bones, add service, drift upmarket, get undercut by the next entrant.
segments.tr: - **#1–3 — Fundamentos:** El comercio minorista es el último paso del canal de distribución, donde el valor se crea mediante *la clasificación, el fraccionamiento de grandes volúmenes, el mantenimiento de inventario y la prestación de servicios*. Los formatos (supermercado, club de almacén, especialidad, de descuento, comercio electrónico) evolucionan a través de la rueda del comercio minorista: entran baratos y básicos, añaden servicio, ascienden en el mercado, son socavados por el siguiente participante.

segments.src: - **#4–6 — Customer and location:** Shopper decision-making, segmentation, and trade-area analysis. Location is retail's most expensive irreversible decision — you can change a price tomorrow, not a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: - **#4–6 — Cliente y ubicación:** Toma de decisiones del comprador, segmentación y análisis del área comercial. La ubicación es la decisión irreversible más cara del comercio minorista: puedes cambiar un precio mañana, no un contrato de arrendamiento de 15 años.

segments.src: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Assortment breadth vs. depth, category management, vendor negotiation, and pricing (cost-plus, competitive, psychological, markdown cadence, EDLP vs. high-low).
segments.tr: - **#7–9 — Comercialización:** Amplitud frente a profundidad del surtido, gestión de categorías, negociación con proveedores y fijación de precios (costo más margen, competitivo, psicológico, cadencia de rebajas, EDLP frente a alto-bajo).

segments.src: - **#10–12 — Operations:** Supply chain and inventory turnover, store layout and visual merchandising, promotion, loyalty, and CRM.
segments.tr: - **#10–12 — Operaciones:** Cadena de suministro y rotación de inventario, diseño de la tienda y comercialización visual, promoción, lealtad y CRM.

segments.src: - **#13–14 — Measurement and channels:** Retail's core metrics and the shift from multichannel to omnichannel to *unified commerce* — one inventory pool, one customer record, many touchpoints.
segments.tr: - **#13–14 — Medición y canales:** Las métricas principales del comercio minorista y el cambio de multicanal a omnicanal y *comercio unificado*: un fondo de inventario, un registro de clientes, muchos puntos de contacto.

segments.src: The one formula worth remembering, in plain text:
segments.tr: La única fórmula que vale la pena recordar, en texto plano:

segments.src: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost
segments.tr: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost

segments.src: It's the discipline of the whole field in one line: retail profit comes from **margin × velocity**, not margin alone.
segments.tr: Es la disciplina de todo el campo en una sola línea: la ganancia minorista proviene del **margen × velocidad**, no solo del margen.

segments.src: A high-margin item that never sells loses to a thin-margin item that turns twelve times a year.
segments.tr: Un artículo de alto margen que nunca se vende pierde ante un artículo de bajo margen que rota doce veces al año.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Retail's frontier is instrumentation — sensing, deciding, selling, and fulfilling are all becoming data loops, with retail media networks the single biggest business-model change.
segments.tr: 1. La frontera del comercio minorista es la instrumentación: la detección, la decisión, la venta y el cumplimiento se están convirtiendo en bucles de datos, siendo las redes de medios minoristas el cambio de modelo de negocio más importante.

segments.src: 2. Policy is not background noise: sales tax nexus, marketplace verification, interchange fees, privacy law, and trade rules each move real money.
segments.tr: 2. La política no es ruido de fondo: el nexo del impuesto sobre las ventas, la verificación de mercado, las tarifas de intercambio, la ley de privacidad y las reglas comerciales mueven dinero real.

segments.src: 3. Underneath it all, the job hasn't changed — right assortment, right place, right price, acceptable cost to serve — and GMROI is still how you know you're doing it.
segments.tr: 3. Debajo de todo, el trabajo no ha cambiado: surtido correcto, lugar correcto, precio correcto, costo aceptable para servir, y el GMROI sigue siendo cómo sabes que lo estás haciendo.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms

segments.tr: - **Red de medios minoristas** — El negocio publicitario propio de un minorista, que vende ubicaciones en su sitio, aplicación y pantallas en la tienda utilizando sus datos de compra de primera mano.

segments.src: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — A digital price display on the shelf edge, updated centrally; its value is driving the cost of a price change toward zero.
segments.tr: - **Etiqueta electrónica de estante (ESL)** — Una pantalla de precios digital en el borde del estante, actualizada centralmente; su valor es llevar el costo de un cambio de precio hacia cero.

segments.src: - **Unified commerce** — A single shared inventory, pricing, and customer record behind every channel, as opposed to separate online and store systems stitched together.
segments.tr: - **Comercio unificado** — Un inventario, precio y registro de clientes compartidos únicos detrás de cada canal, en lugar de sistemas separados en línea y en tienda unidos.

segments.src: - **Economic nexus** — The rule, established for sales tax by *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, that a seller can owe tax collection duties in a state based on sales volume there, without a physical location.
segments.tr: - **Nexo económico** — La regla, establecida para el impuesto sobre las ventas por *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, de que un vendedor puede deber obligaciones de recaudación de impuestos en un estado en función del volumen de ventas allí, sin una ubicación física.

segments.src: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Gross margin dollars per dollar of inventory carried; retail's core test of whether margin and turnover are working together.
segments.tr: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment / Retorno del margen bruto sobre la inversión en inventario)** — Dólares de margen bruto por dólar de inventario retenido; la prueba central del comercio minorista de si el margen y la rotación están funcionando juntos.

ar.title: [تجارة التجزئة 101 #15] المتجر يتحول إلى برمجيات — وفصلك الدراسي بأكمله في صفحة واحدة

segments.src: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.
segments.tr: > يتم كتابة عقد التجزئة القادم بواسطة قوتين لا يراهما معظم المتسوقين أبدًا — التكنولوجيا التي تحول المتجر إلى نظام بيانات، والسياسة التي تحدد بهدوء قواعد الرف. إليك إلى أين يتجه القطاع، بالإضافة إلى ملخص من صفحة واحدة لكل ما غطته هذه السلسلة.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.
segments.tr: طوال معظم تاريخها، كانت تجارة التجزئة نشاطًا **ماديًا** يصادف احتفاظه بالسجلات.

segments.src: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.
segments.tr: اليوم أصبحت نشاطًا **معلوماتيًا** يصادف امتلاكه لمبانٍ.

segments.src: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.
segments.tr: هذا العكس الفردي يفسر كل اتجاه تقريبًا في الأفق.

segments.src: Break it into three layers.
segments.tr: قم بتقسيمها إلى ثلاث طبقات.

segments.src: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**
segments.tr: تكنولوجيا التجزئة ("ريتيل تك") — المتجر يصبح مزودًا بالأجهزة.

segments.src: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."
segments.tr: النمط ليس "الروبوتات تستبدل الموظفين".

segments.src: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:
segments.tr: بل إن كل خطوة في سلسلة التجزئة تحصل على مستشعر وحلقة تغذية مرتدة:

segments.src: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.
segments.tr: - **الاستشعار:** علامات تحديد الهوية بموجات الراديو (RFID)، كاميرات رؤية الكمبيوتر، والرفوف الذكية تحول "نعتقد أن لدينا 40 وحدة" إلى "نعرف أن لدينا 37، و3 في الممر الخطأ". دقة المخزون في قطاع الملابس ظلت تاريخياً أقل بكثير من 100%، وسد هذه الفجوة يساوي أموالاً حقيقية — لا يمكنك بيع ما يظن نظامك أنه مفقود.

segments.src: - **Deciding:** Machine-learning demand forecasting, automated replenishment, and algorithmic pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.
segments.tr: - **اتخاذ القرار:** التنبؤ بالطلب التعلم الآلي، التجديد الآلي، التسعير الخوارزمي. تسميات الرفوف الإلكترونية (ESLs) تهم هنا ليس لأن الأسعار تتغير كل ساعة (معظم السلسلات تغيرها نادراً، وفعل ذلك بشكل عدواني يجذب رد فعل عكسي)، ولكن لأن *تكلفة تغيير السعر* تنخفض إلى ما يقرب من الصفر. عندما يصبح القرار رخيصاً، فإنك تتخذه بشكل متكرر.

segments.src: - **Selling:** Retail media networks — retailers selling ad space on their own sites, apps, and screens using their own purchase data. This is the most important business-model shift of the last decade. Amazon's advertising business alone runs in the tens of billions of dollars a year, and Walmart, Kroger, Target, and even gas-station chains now run their own. Why it matters: ad revenue carries far higher margins than selling groceries, so it can subsidize low prices. The retailer's real product starts to include *access to its shoppers*.
segments.tr: - **البيع:** شبكات وسائل الإعلام للتجزئة — تجار التجزئة يبيعون مساحات إعلانية على مواقعهم وتطبيقاتهم وشاشاتهم الخاصة باستخدام بيانات الشراء الخاصة بهم. هذا هو أهم تحول في نموذج الأعمال في العقد الماضي. أعمال الإعلانات وحدها لأمازون تعمل بعشرات المليارات من الدولارات سنوياً، ووول مارت، وكروجر، وتارجت، وحتى سلاسل محطات الوقود تدير الآن أعمالها الخاصة. لماذا يهم: عائدات الإعلانات تحمل هوامش أعلى بكثير من بيع البقالة، لذا يمكنها دعم الأسعار المنخفضة. يبدأ المنتج الحقيقي لتاجر التجزئة في تضمين *الوصول إلى متسوقيه*.

segments.src: - **Fulfilling:** Micro-fulfillment, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery. Note the honest part — these are expensive. Fulfilling a $40 online grocery order costs far more than letting a customer walk the aisles and do the picking for free.
segments.tr: - **التنفيذ:** التنفيذ المصغر، الاستلام من الرصيف، والتوصيل في نفس اليوم. لاحظ الجزء الصادق — هذه مكلفة. تنفيذ طلب بقالة عبر الإنترنت بقيمة 40 دولاراً يكلف أكثر بكثير من السماح للعميل بالسير في الممرات والقيام بالقطف مجاناً.

segments.src: Two cautionary notes, because hype is not analysis.
segments.tr: ملاحظتان تحذيريتان، لأن الضجة ليست تحليلاً.

segments.src: **Self-checkout** expanded fast, then several chains pulled it back or restricted it after shrink and customer-experience problems.
segments.tr: **الدفع الذاتي** توسع بسرعة، ثم تراجعت عدة سلاسل عنه أو تقييده بعد مشاكل الانكماش وتجربة العملاء.

segments.src: **Fully autonomous "just walk out" stores** proved harder and costlier than early demos suggested; Amazon scaled back the format in its larger grocery stores.
segments.tr: **المتاجر المستقلة تماماً "فقط امشِ واخرج"** ثبت أنها أكثر صعوبة وتكلفة مما اقترحت العروض التوضيحية المبكرة؛ قللت أمازون من حجم التنسيق في متاجر البقالة الأكبر الخاصة بها.

segments.src: The lesson from Lesson #2's *wheel of retailing* still holds: technology changes the cost curve, but it doesn't repeal the economics.
segments.tr: الدرس من *عجلة التجارة بالتجزئة* للدرس رقم 2 لا يزال سارياً: التكنولوجيا تغير منحنى التكلفة، لكنها لا تلغي الاقتصاديات.

segments.src: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**
segments.tr: سياسة التجزئة — كتاب القواعد غير المرئي.

segments.src: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:
segments.tr: يعمل تجار التجزئة ضمن قيود تحددها المحاكم والهيئات التشريعية، وتغيير القاعدة يمكن أن يحرك ربحاً أكثر من أي قرار تجاري:

segments.src: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.
segments.tr: - **ضريبة المبيعات:** *ساوث داكوتا ضد وايفير* (2018) سمحت للولايات بمطالبة بائعي التجزئة عبر الإنترنت من خارج الولاية بجمع ضريبة المبيعات. لقد أنهت ميزة سعرية هيكلية للتجارة الإلكترونية بين عشية وضحاها.

segments.src: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.
segments.tr: - **مساءلة السوق:** قانون إعلام المستهلكين (المطبق منذ عام 2023) يتطلب من الأسواق عبر الإنترنت التحقق من بائعي الطرف الثالث ذوي الحجم الكبير — ردا على جرائم التجزئة المنظمة والسلع المقلدة.

segments.src: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.
segments.tr: - **المدفوعات:** رسوم تبادل البطاقات ("التمرير") هي واحدة من أكبر بنود التكلفة لتاجر التجزئة بعد العمالة والإيجار، وكانت موضوع سنوات من التقاضي والمقترحات التشريعية المتكررة.

segments.src: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.
segments.tr: - **الخصوصية:** قوانين الولاية التي تقودها CCPA/CPRA في كاليفورنيا، بالإضافة إلى أكثر من عشرة قوانين أخرى، تقيد كيفية جمع واستخدام بيانات المتسوقين الكامنة وراء وسائل الإعلام للتجزئة.

segments.src: - **Trade:** Tariffs and the treatment of low-value imported parcels (the "de minimis" exemption) have tightened in recent years — a reminder that one customs rule can reshape an entire business model, as it did for ultra-low-price direct-from-overseas apps.
segments.tr: - **التجارة:** التعريفات الجمركية ومعاملة الطرود المستوردة منخفضة القيمة (إعفاء "de minimis") قد شددت في السنوات الأخيرة — تذكير بأن قاعدة جمركية واحدة يمكن أن تعيد تشكيل نموذج أعمال كامل، كما فعلت لتطبيقات الأسعار الزهيدة المباشرة من الخارج.

segments.src: - **Labor and sustainability:** Minimum wage, scheduling laws, and packaging/extended-producer-responsibility rules all land directly on store P&Ls.
segments.tr: - **العمالة والاستدامة:** الحد الأدنى للأجور، قوانين جدولة العمل، وقواعد التغليف/مسؤولية المنتجين الممتدة كلها تهبط مباشرة على بيانات الأرباح والخسائر للمتجر.

segments.src: What actually stays constant.**
segments.tr: ما يبقى ثابتاً في الواقع.

segments.src: Strip away the tech and the same job remains: *get the right assortment, to the right place, at the right price, at an acceptable cost to serve.* Every trend above is a new way to do that old job — or a new constraint on doing it.
segments.tr: قم بإزالة التكنولوجيا ويبقى نفس الوظيفة: *احصل على التشكيلة الصحيحة، في المكان الصحيح، بالسعر الصحيح، بتكلفة مقبولة للخدمة.* كل اتجاه أعلاه هو طريقة جديدة للقيام بهذه الوظيفة القديمة — أو قيد جديد على القيام بها.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: You're at a Target in Columbus, Ohio, buying a $12.99 bottle of laundry detergent.
segments.tr: أنت في متجر تارجت في كولومبوس، أوهايو، تشتري زجاجة مسحوق غسيل بقيمة 12.99 دولاراً.

segments.src: Trace what just touched that purchase.
segments.tr: تتبع ما للتو لمس هذا الشراء.

segments.src: You searched "detergent" in the app — the top result was a **sponsored placement** paid for by a brand through Target's retail media network.
segments.tr: لقد بحثت عن "مسحوق غسيل" في التطبيق — النتيجة الأولى كانت **موضعاً ممولاً** تم دفع ثمنه بواسطة علامة تجارية عبر شبكة وسائل الإعلام للتجزئة الخاصة بتارجت.

segments.src: The app said the item was in Aisle D24 because an **inventory system** thinks that's where it is.
segments.tr: أفاد التطبيق أن العنصر كان في الممر D24 لأن **نظام المخزون** يعتقد أن هذا هو مكانه.

segments.src: The shelf price came from an **electronic label**, and it matched the app because unified pricing systems are table stakes now.
segments.tr: جاء سعر الرف من **ملصق إلكتروني**، وتطابق مع التطبيق لأن أنظمة التسعير الموحدة هي الشروط الأساسية الآن.

segments.src: You paid with a card; roughly 2–3% of that $12.99 left the retailer as an **interchange fee**.
segments.tr: دفعْتَ ببطاقة؛ ما يقرب من 2-3% من تلك 12.99 دولارًا غادرت بائع التجزئة كـ **رسوم تبادل**.

segments.src: Sales tax was collected — and would have been collected identically if you'd ordered it online from an out-of-state seller, thanks to *Wayfair*.
segments.tr: تم جمع ضريبة المبيعات — وكان سيتم جمعها بشكل مطبق تماماً إذا كنت قد طلبتها عبر الإنترنت من بائع خارج الولاية، بفضل *وايفير*.

segments.src: When you scanned out at self-checkout, a camera-based system was watching for scan avoidance.
segments.tr: عندما قمت بالمسح عند الدفع الذاتي، كان هناك نظام قائم على الكاميرا يراقب تجنب المسح.

segments.src: Overnight, an **automated replenishment algorithm** will decide whether to reorder, and the data from your basket will help price the next brand's ad slot.
segments.tr: بين عشية وضحاها، ستحدد **خوارزمية تجديد آلية** ما إذا كان سيتم إعادة الطلب، والبيانات من سلتك ستساعد في تسعير فتحة إعلان العلامة التجارية التالية.

segments.src: One bottle of detergent.
segments.tr: زجاجة واحدة من مسحوق الغسيل.

segments.src: At least six of the technologies and policies above were involved, and you saw exactly none of them.
segments.tr: على الأقل ست تقنيات وسياسات من المذكورة أعلاه كانت متضمنة، ولم ترَ أيًا منها على الإطلاق.

segments.src: ## The Whole Series in Three Minutes
segments.tr: ## السلسلة بأكملها في ثلاث دقائق

segments.src: - **#1–3 — Foundations:** Retailing is the last step of the distribution channel, where value is created through *sorting, breaking bulk, holding inventory, and providing service*. Formats (supermarket, warehouse club, specialty, off-price, e-commerce) evolve through the wheel of retailing: enter cheap and bare-bones, add service, drift upmarket, get undercut by the next entrant.
segments.tr: - **#1-3 — الأسس:** تجارة التجزئة هي الخطوة الأخيرة من قناة التوزيع، حيث يتم إنشاء القيمة من خلال *الفرز، وتكسير الدفعات الكبيرة، والاحتفاظ بالمخزون، وتوفير الخدمة*. تتطور التنسيقات (السوبر ماركت، نادي المستودعات، التخصصي، الأسعار المخفضة، التجارة الإلكترونية) عبر عجلة تجارة التجزئة: الدخول برخيص وبأقل الإمكانيات، إضافة الخدمة، الانجراف نحو الفئات الراقية، والحصول على تقويض من الداخل التالي.

segments.src: - **#4–6 — Customer and location:** Shopper decision-making, segmentation, and trade-area analysis. Location is retail's most expensive irreversible decision — you can change a price tomorrow, not a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: - **#4-6 — العميل والموقع:** اتخاذ القرار للمسوق، التقسيم، وتحليل منطقة التجارة. الموقع هو أغلى قرار لا رجعة فيه في التجزئة — يمكنك تغيير السعر غداً، وليس عقد إيجار لمدة 15 عاماً.

segments.src: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Assortment breadth vs. depth, category management, vendor negotiation, and pricing (cost-plus, competitive, psychological, markdown cadence, EDLP vs. high-low).
segments.tr: - **#7-9 — التجارة والترويج:** اتساع التشكيلة مقابل العمق، إدارة الفئات، مفاوضات البائعين، والتسعير (التكلفة مضاف إليها هامش، تنافسي، نفسي، وتيرة التخفيضات، الأسعار المنخفضة اليومية مقابل المرتفعة-المنخفضة).

segments.src: - **#10–12 — Operations:** Supply chain and inventory turnover, store layout and visual merchandising, promotion, loyalty, and CRM.
segments.tr: - **#10-12 — العمليات:** سلسلة التوريد ودوران المخزون، تخطيط المتجر والتسويق البصري، الترويج، الولاء، وإدارة علاقات العملاء (CRM).

segments.src: - **#13–14 — Measurement and channels:** Retail's core metrics and the shift from multichannel to omnichannel to *unified commerce* — one inventory pool, one customer record, many touchpoints.
segments.tr: - **#13-14 — القياس والقنوات:** مقاييس التجزئة الأساسية والتحول من القنوات المتعددة إلى القنوات الشاملة إلى *التجارة الموحدة* — مجموعة مخزون واحدة، سجل عملاء واحد، العديد من نقاط الاتصال.

segments.src: The one formula worth remembering, in plain text:
segments.tr: الصيغة الوحيدة التي تستحق التذكر، بالنص البسيط:

segments.src: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost
segments.tr: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost

segments.src: It's the discipline of the whole field in one line: retail profit comes from **margin × velocity**, not margin alone.
segments.tr: إنه منضبط المجال بأكمله في سطر واحد: ربح التجزئة يأتي من **هامش الربح × السرعة**، وليس الهامش وحده.

segments.src: A high-margin item that never sells loses to a thin-margin item that turns twelve times a year.
segments.tr: عنصر ذو هامش ربح مرتفع لا يُباع أبداً يخسر أمام عنصر ذو هامش منخفض يدور اثنتي عشرة مرة في السنة.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## ملخص من ثلاثة أسطر

segments.src: 1. Retail's frontier is instrumentation — sensing, deciding, selling, and fulfilling are all becoming data loops, with retail media networks the single biggest business-model change.
segments.tr: 1. حدود تجارة التجزئة هي الأدوات — الاستشعار، واتخاذ القرار، والبيع، والتنفيذ كلها تصبح حلقات بيانات، حيث تعد شبكات وسائل الإعلام للتجزئة التغيير الأكبر في نموذج الأعمال.

segments.src: 2. Policy is not background noise: sales tax nexus, marketplace verification, interchange fees, privacy law, and trade rules each move real money.
segments.tr: 2. السياسة ليست ضوضاء في الخلفية: صلة ضريبة المبيعات، والتحقق من السوق، ورسوم التبادل، وقانون الخصوصية، وقواعد التجارة، كل منها يحرك أموالاً حقيقية.

segments.src: 3. Underneath it all, the job hasn't changed — right assortment, right place, right price, acceptable cost to serve — and GMROI is still how you know you're doing it.
segments.tr: 3. تحت كل ذلك، الوظيفة لم تتغير — التشكيلة الصحيحة، المكان الصحيح، السعر الصحيح، التكلفة المقبولة للخدمة — و GMROI لا يزال هو كيف تعرف أنك تفعل ذلك.

segments.tr: ## ✅ اختبار ذاتي

segments.tr: - أ) رابطة تجارية تشارك بيانات المبيعات بين تجار التجزئة المتنافسين

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Retail media network** — A retailer's own advertising business, selling placements on its site, app, and in-store screens using its first-party purchase data.
segments.tr: - **شبكة وسائل الإعلام للتجزئة** — أعمال الإعلانات الخاصة ببطاقة التجزئة، وبيع المساحات الإعلانية على موقعها، وتطبيقها، وشاشات المتجر باستخدام بيانات الشراء الخاصة بها من الطرف الأول.

segments.src: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — A digital price display on the shelf edge, updated centrally; its value is driving the cost of a price change toward zero.
segments.tr: - **تسمية الرف الإلكتروني (ESL)** — عرض أسعار رقمي على حافة الرف، يتم تحديثه مركزياً؛ قيمته تدفع تكلفة تغيير السعر نحو الصفر.

segments.src: - **Unified commerce** — A single shared inventory, pricing, and customer record behind every channel, as opposed to separate online and store systems stitched together.
segments.tr: - **التجارة الموحدة** — مخزون واحد مشترك، وتسعير، وسجل عملاء وراء كل قناة، على عكس أنظمة الإنترنت والمتاجر المنفصلة المخاطة ببعضها.

segments.src: - **Economic nexus** — The rule, established for sales tax by *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, that a seller can owe tax collection duties in a state based on sales volume there, without a physical location.
segments.tr: - **الصلة الاقتصادية** — القاعدة، التي أُسست لضريبة المبيعات بواسطة *ساوث داكوتا ضد وايفير*، بأن البائع يمكن أن يدين بواجبات تحصيل الضرائب في ولاية بناءً على حجم المبيعات هناك، بدون موقع مادي.

segments.src: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Gross margin dollars per dollar of inventory carried; retail's core test of whether margin and turnover are working together.
segments.tr: - **GMROI (عائد الهامش الإجمالي على استثمار المخزون)** — دولارات الهامش الإجمالي لكل دولار من المخزون المحتفظ به؛ اختبار تجارة التجزئة الأساسي لما إذا كان الهامش والدوران يعملان معاً.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** A retail media network is the retailer monetizing its own audience and purchase data; the high margins on that ad revenue can subsidize lower shelf prices.
segments.tr: *الإجابات: **س1 — ب.** شبكة وسائل الإعلام للتجزئة هي قيام بائع التجزئة بتحقيق الدخل من جمهوره وبيانات الشراء الخاصة به؛ الهوامش العالية على عائدات الإعلانات تلك يمكن أن تدعم أسعار الرفوف الأقل.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** Frequent demand-based price hikes invite consumer and political backlash, and most chains avoid them.
segments.tr: **س2 — خطأ (False).** الزيادات المتكررة في الأسعار القائمة على الطلب تجتذب رد فعل عكسي استهلاكي وسياسي، ومعظم السلاسل تتجنبها.

segments.src: The real value is operational: near-zero cost per price change, plus shelf-to-app price consistency and less labor spent on paper tags.
segments.tr: القيمة الحقيقية تشغيلية: تكلفة قريبة من الصفر لكل تغيير في السعر، بالإضافة إلى اتساق سعر الرف إلى التطبيق وتقليل العمالة المنفقة على العلامات الورقية.

segments.src: **Q3 — C.** Before Wayfair, many remote online sellers weren't required to collect state sales tax, effectively making their prices several percent cheaper than a local store's.
segments.tr: **س3 — ج.** قبل وايفير، لم يُطلب من العديد من بائعي التجزئة عن بعد عبر الإنترنت جمع ضريبة مبيعات الولاية، مما جعل أسعارهم أرخص بعدة بالمائة بفعالية من أسعار المتجر المحلي.
