fr.title: [Retailing 101 #15] Le magasin devient logiciel — et tout votre semestre sur une seule page

segments.src: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.
segments.tr: > La prochaine décennie de la vente au détail est façonnée par deux forces que la plupart des acheteurs ne voient jamais : la technologie qui transforme le magasin en un système de données, et la réglementation qui établit discrètement les règles des rayons. Voici où se dirige l'industrie, ainsi qu'un récapitulatif en une seule page de tout ce que cette série a couvert.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept du jour

segments.src: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.
segments.tr: Pendant la majeure partie de son histoire, la vente au détail était une entreprise **physique** qui tenait des registres.

segments.src: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.
segments.tr: Aujourd'hui, c'est une entreprise **d'information** qui se trouve avoir des bâtiments.

segments.src: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.
segments.tr: Cette simple inversion explique presque toutes les tendances à l'horizon.

segments.src: Break it into three layers.
segments.tr: Décomposons cela en trois couches.

segments.src: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**
segments.tr: Technologie de la vente au détail ("retailtech") — le magasin devient instrumenté.**

segments.src: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."
segments.tr: Le schéma n'est pas "les robots remplacent les employés".

segments.src: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:
segments.tr: C'est que chaque étape de la chaîne de vente au détail se dote d'un capteur et d'une boucle de rétroaction :

segments.src: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.
segments.tr: - **Détection :** Les étiquettes RFID, les caméras de vision par ordinateur et les étagères intelligentes transforment "nous pensons avoir 40 unités" en "nous savons que nous en avons 37, et 3 sont dans la mauvaise allée". La précision des stocks dans l'habillement a historiquement oscillé bien en dessous de 100 %, et combler cet écart vaut de l'argent réel — vous ne pouvez pas vendre ce que votre système croit manquant.

segments.src: - **Deciding:** Machine-learning demand forecasting, automated replenishment, and algorithmic pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.
segments.tr: - **Décision :** Prévision de la demande par apprentissage automatique, réapprovisionnement automatisé et tarification algorithmique. Les étiquettes électroniques de gondole (ESL) comptent ici non pas parce que les prix changent toutes les heures (la plupart des chaînes les changent rarement, et le faire de manière agressive suscite des réactions négatives), mais parce que le *coût de modification d'un prix* tombe presque à zéro. Lorsqu'une décision devient bon marché, vous la prenez plus souvent.

segments.src: - **Selling:** Retail media networks — retailers selling ad space on their own sites, apps, and screens using their own purchase data. This is the most important business-model shift of the last decade. Amazon's advertising business alone runs in the tens of billions of dollars a year, and Walmart, Kroger, Target, and even gas-station chains now run their own. Why it matters: ad revenue carries far higher margins than selling groceries, so it can subsidize low prices. The retailer's real product starts to include *access to its shoppers*.
segments.tr: - **Vente :** Les réseaux médias de vente au détail — les détaillants vendant des espaces publicitaires sur leurs propres sites, applications et écrans en utilisant leurs propres données d'achat. Il s'agit du changement de modèle commercial le plus important de la dernière décennie. L'activité publicitaire d'Amazon à elle seule se chiffre en dizaines de milliards de dollars par an, et Walmart, Kroger, Target et même les chaînes de stations-service exploitent désormais la leur. Pourquoi c'est important : les revenus publicitaires génèrent des marges bien plus élevées que la vente de produits d'épicerie, ce qui permet de subventionner des prix bas. Le véritable produit du commerce commence à inclure *l'accès à ses acheteurs*.

segments.src: - **Fulfilling:** Micro-fulfillment, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery. Note the honest part — these are expensive. Fulfilling a $40 online grocery order costs far more than letting a customer walk the aisles and do the picking for free.
segments.tr: - **Exécution :** Micro-exécution, ramassage en bord de trottoir et livraison le jour même. Notez la partie honnête — ceux-ci sont coûteux. Exécuter une commande d'épicerie en ligne de 40 $ coûte beaucoup plus cher que de laisser un client parcourir les allées et faire la sélection gratuitement.

segments.src: Two cautionary notes, because hype is not analysis.
segments.tr: Deux notes de mise en garde, car le battage médiatique n'est pas une analyse.

segments.src: **Self-checkout** expanded fast, then several chains pulled it back or restricted it after shrink and customer-experience problems.
segments.tr: L'**auto-caisse** s'est développée rapidement, puis plusieurs chaînes l'ont retirée ou restreinte après des problèmes de démarque inconnue et d'expérience client.

segments.src: **Fully autonomous "just walk out" stores** proved harder and costlier than early demos suggested; Amazon scaled back the format in its larger grocery stores.
segments.tr: Les **magasins entièrement autonomes "sans caisse"** se sont avérés plus difficiles et plus coûteux que ne le suggéraient les premières démonstrations ; Amazon a réduit le format dans ses plus grands magasins d'alimentation.

segments.src: The lesson from Lesson #2's *wheel of retailing* still holds: technology changes the cost curve, but it doesn't repeal the economics.
segments.tr: La leçon de la leçon n° 2 sur la *roue de la distribution* tient toujours : la technologie modifie la courbe des coûts, mais elle n'abroge pas l'économie.

segments.src: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**
segments.tr: Politique de vente au détail — le livre de règles invisible.**

segments.src: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:
segments.tr: Les détaillants opèrent dans les limites fixées par les tribunaux et les législations, et un changement de règle peut déplacer plus de profits que n'importe quelle décision de marchandisage :

segments.src: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.
segments.tr: - **Taxe de vente :** *South Dakota c. Wayfair* (2018) a permis aux États d'exiger des vendeurs en ligne hors État qu'ils perçoivent la taxe de vente. Cela a mis fin du jour au lendemain à un avantage de prix structurel pour le commerce électronique.

segments.src: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.
segments.tr: - **Responsabilité des plateformes :** La loi INFORM Consumers Act (en vigueur depuis 2023) exige des marchés en ligne qu'ils vérifient les vendeurs tiers à grand volume — une réponse à la criminalité organisée dans le commerce de détail et aux produits contrefaits.

segments.src: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.
segments.tr: - **Paiements :** Les frais d'interchange (« swipe fees ») des cartes sont l'un des postes de dépenses les plus importants d'un détaillant après la main-d'œuvre et le loyer, et ils ont fait l'objet d'années de litiges et de propositions législatives répétées.

segments.src: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.
segments.tr: - **Confidentialité :** Les lois des États menées par le CCPA/CPRA de la Californie, ainsi que plus d'une dizaine d'autres, limitent la manière dont les données des acheteurs derrière les médias de vente au détail peuvent être collectées et utilisées.

segments.src: - **Trade:** Tariffs and the treatment of low-value imported parcels (the "de minimis" exemption) have tightened in recent years — a reminder that one customs rule can reshape an entire business model, as it did for ultra-low-price direct-from-overseas apps.
segments.tr: - **Commerce :** Les tarifs douaniers et le traitement des colis importés de faible valeur (l'exemption « de minimis ») se sont durcis ces dernières années — un rappel qu'une seule règle douanière peut remodeler tout un modèle d'entreprise, comme cela a été le cas pour les applications ultra-bon marché directement venues d'outre-mer.

segments.src: - **Labor and sustainability:** Minimum wage, scheduling laws, and packaging/extended-producer-responsibility rules all land directly on store P&Ls.
segments.tr: - **Travail et durabilité :** Le salaire minimum, les lois sur les horaires et les règles d'emballage et de responsabilité élargie du producteur pèsent tous directement sur les comptes de résultat des magasins.

segments.src: What actually stays constant.**
segments.tr: Ce qui reste constant.**

segments.src: Strip away the tech and the same job remains: *get the right assortment, to the right place, at the right price, at an acceptable cost to serve.* Every trend above is a new way to do that old job — or a new constraint on doing it.
segments.tr: Retirez la technologie et le même travail demeure : *obtenir le bon assortiment, au bon endroit, au bon prix, à un coût de service acceptable.* Chaque tendance ci-dessus est une nouvelle façon de faire ce vieux travail — ou une nouvelle contrainte pour le faire.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie de tous les jours

segments.src: You're at a Target in Columbus, Ohio, buying a $12.99 bottle of laundry detergent.
segments.tr: Vous êtes dans un Target à Columbus, dans l'Ohio, en train d'acheter une bouteille de détergent à linge de 12,99 $.

segments.src: Trace what just touched that purchase.
segments.tr: Retracez ce qui vient de toucher cet achat.

segments.src: You searched "detergent" in the app — the top result was a **sponsored placement** paid for by a brand through Target's retail media network.
segments.tr: Vous avez recherché "detergent" dans l'application — le premier résultat était un **placement sponsorisé** payé par une marque par l'intermédiaire du réseau média de vente au détail de Target.

segments.src: The app said the item was in Aisle D24 because an **inventory system** thinks that's where it is.
segments.tr: L'application indiquait que l'article se trouvait dans l'allée D24 parce qu'un **système d'inventaire** pense que c'est là qu'il est.

segments.src: The shelf price came from an **electronic label**, and it matched the app because unified pricing systems are table stakes now.
segments.tr: Le prix en rayon provenait d'une **étiquette électronique**, et il correspondait à l'application parce que les systèmes de tarification unifiés sont désormais incontournables.

segments.src: You paid with a card; roughly 2–3% of that $12.99 left the retailer as an **interchange fee**.
segments.tr: Vous avez payé avec une carte ; environ 2 à 3 % de ces 12,99 $ ont quitté le détaillant sous forme de **frais d'interchange**.

segments.src: Sales tax was collected — and would have been collected identically if you'd ordered it online from an out-of-state seller, thanks to *Wayfair*.
segments.tr: La taxe de vente a été perçue — et l'aurait été de manière identique si vous l'aviez commandé en ligne auprès d'un vendeur hors État, grâce à *Wayfair*.

segments.src: When you scanned out at self-checkout, a camera-based system was watching for scan avoidance.
segments.tr: Lorsque vous avez scanné votre sortie à la caisse automatique, un système basé sur des caméras surveillait l'évitement du scan.

segments.src: Overnight, an **automated replenishment algorithm** will decide whether to reorder, and the data from your basket will help price the next brand's ad slot.
segments.tr: Pendant la nuit, un **algorithme de réapprovisionnement automatisé** décidera s'il faut recommander, et les données de votre panier aideront à tarifer l'espace publicitaire de la prochaine marque.

segments.tr: Une bouteille de détergent.

segments.src: At least six of the technologies and policies above were involved, and you saw exactly none of them.
segments.tr: Au moins six des technologies et politiques ci-dessus étaient impliquées, et vous n'en avez vu absolument aucune.

segments.src: ## The Whole Series in Three Minutes
segments.tr: ## Toute la série en trois minutes

segments.src: - **#1–3 — Foundations:** Retailing is the last step of the distribution channel, where value is created through *sorting, breaking bulk, holding inventory, and providing service*. Formats (supermarket, warehouse club, specialty, off-price, e-commerce) evolve through the wheel of retailing: enter cheap and bare-bones, add service, drift upmarket, get undercut by the next entrant.
segments.tr: - **#1–3 — Fondations :** La vente au détail est la dernière étape du canal de distribution, où de la valeur est créée par *le tri, le fractionnement des lots, la détention de stocks et la fourniture de services*. Les formats (supermarché, club-entrepôt, spécialisé, soldeur, commerce électronique) évoluent à travers la roue de la distribution : entrée à bas coût et minimaliste, ajout de services, montée en gamme, éviction par le nouveau venu suivant.

segments.src: - **#4–6 — Customer and location:** Shopper decision-making, segmentation, and trade-area analysis. Location is retail's most expensive irreversible decision — you can change a price tomorrow, not a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: - **#4–6 — Client et emplacement :** Prise de décision de l'acheteur, segmentation et analyse de la zone de chalandise. L'emplacement est la décision irréversible la plus coûteuse du commerce de détail — vous pouvez changer un prix demain, pas un bail de 15 ans.

segments.src: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Assortment breadth vs. depth, category management, vendor negotiation, and pricing (cost-plus, competitive, psychological, markdown cadence, EDLP vs. high-low).
segments.tr: - **#7–9 — Merchandising :** Largeur vs profondeur de l'assortiment, gestion par catégorie, négociation avec les fournisseurs et tarification (coût majoré, concurrentiel, psychologique, cadence des démarques, EDLP vs haut-bas).

segments.src: - **#10–12 — Operations:** Supply chain and inventory turnover, store layout and visual merchandising, promotion, loyalty, and CRM.
segments.tr: - **#10–12 — Opérations :** Chaîne d'approvisionnement et rotation des stocks, agencement du magasin et marchandisage visuel, promotion, fidélisation et gestion de la relation client (CRM).

segments.src: - **#13–14 — Measurement and channels:** Retail's core metrics and the shift from multichannel to omnichannel to *unified commerce* — one inventory pool, one customer record, many touchpoints.
segments.tr: - **#13–14 — Mesure et canaux :** Les mesures clés du commerce de détail et le passage du multicanal à l'omicanal puis au *commerce unifié* — un pool de stocks, un dossier client, de nombreux points de contact.

segments.src: The one formula worth remembering, in plain text:
segments.tr: La seule formule qui vaut la peine d'être retenue, en texte brut :

segments.src: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost
segments.tr: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost

segments.src: It's the discipline of the whole field in one line: retail profit comes from **margin × velocity**, not margin alone.
segments.tr: C'est la discipline de tout le domaine en une seule ligne : le profit du commerce de détail provient de **la marge × la vitesse**, et non de la marge seule.

segments.src: A high-margin item that never sells loses to a thin-margin item that turns twelve times a year.
segments.tr: Un article à forte marge qui ne se vend jamais perd face à un article à faible marge qui tourne douze fois par an.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en trois lignes

segments.src: 1. Retail's frontier is instrumentation — sensing, deciding, selling, and fulfilling are all becoming data loops, with retail media networks the single biggest business-model change.
segments.tr: 1. La frontière du commerce de détail est l'instrumentation — la détection, la décision, la vente et l'exécution deviennent toutes des boucles de données, les réseaux médias de vente au détail constituant le plus grand changement de modèle commercial.

segments.src: 2. Policy is not background noise: sales tax nexus, marketplace verification, interchange fees, privacy law, and trade rules each move real money.
segments.tr: 2. La politique n'est pas un bruit de fond : le lien de la taxe de vente, la vérification des marchés, les frais d'interchange, la loi sur la confidentialité et les règles commerciales brassent chacun de l'argent réel.

segments.src: 3. Underneath it all, the job hasn't changed — right assortment, right place, right price, acceptable cost to serve — and GMROI is still how you know you're doing it.
segments.tr: 3. Sous tout cela, le travail n'a pas changé — bon assortiment, bon endroit, bon prix, coût de service acceptable — et le GMROI est toujours la façon de savoir que vous le faites bien.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termes du jour

segments.src: - **Retail media network** — A retailer's own advertising business, selling placements on its site, app, and in-store screens using its first-party purchase data.
segments.tr: - **Réseau média de vente au détail (Retail media network)** — La propre entreprise publicitaire d'un détaillant, vendant des emplacements sur son site, son application et ses écrans en magasin en utilisant ses données d'achat de première main.

segments.src: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — A digital price display on the shelf edge, updated centrally; its value is driving the cost of a price change toward zero.
segments.tr: - **Étiquette électronique de gondole (ESL)** — Un affichage numérique des prix sur le bord de l'étagère, mis à jour de manière centralisée ; sa valeur est de réduire le coût d'un changement de prix vers zéro.

segments.src: - **Unified commerce** — A single shared inventory, pricing, and customer record behind every channel, as opposed to separate online and store systems stitched together.
segments.tr: - **Commerce unifié** — Un inventaire, une tarification et un dossier client uniques et partagés derrière chaque canal, par opposition à des systèmes en ligne et en magasin séparés cousus ensemble.

segments.src: - **Economic nexus** — The rule, established for sales tax by *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, that a seller can owe tax collection duties in a state based on sales volume there, without a physical location.
segments.tr: - **Lien économique** — La règle, établie pour la taxe de vente par *South Dakota c. Wayfair*, selon laquelle un vendeur peut avoir des obligations de perception de taxes dans un État en fonction du volume des ventes qui y sont réalisées, sans emplacement physique.

segments.src: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Gross margin dollars per dollar of inventory carried; retail's core test of whether margin and turnover are working together.
segments.tr: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Dollars de marge brute par dollar de stock détenu ; le test fondamental du commerce de détail pour savoir si la marge et la rotation fonctionnent ensemble.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** A retail media network is the retailer monetizing its own audience and purchase data; the high margins on that ad revenue can subsidize lower shelf prices.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** Frequent demand-based price hikes invite consumer and political backlash, and most chains avoid them.

segments.src: The real value is operational: near-zero cost per price change, plus shelf-to-app price consistency and less labor spent on paper tags.

segments.src: **Q3 — C.** Before Wayfair, many remote online sellers weren't required to collect state sales tax, effectively making their prices several percent cheaper than a local store's.

pt.title: [Retailing 101 #15] A Loja Está Se Tornando Software — e Todo o Seu Semestre em Uma Página

segments.src: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.
segments.tr: > A próxima década do varejo está sendo escrita por duas forças que a maioria dos compradores nunca vê — a tecnologia que transforma a loja em um sistema de dados e a política que define silenciosamente as regras da gôndola. Aqui está para onde a indústria está indo, além de um resumo de uma página de tudo o que esta série cobriu.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.
segments.tr: Para a maior parte de sua história, o varejo foi um negócio **físico** que por acaso mantinha registros.

segments.src: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.
segments.tr: Hoje é um negócio de **informação** que por acaso tem edifícios.

segments.src: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.
segments.tr: Essa única inversão explica quase todas as tendências no horizonte.

segments.src: Break it into three layers.
segments.tr: Divida em três camadas.

segments.src: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**
segments.tr: Tecnologia de varejo ("retailtech") — a loja se torna instrumentada.**

segments.src: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."
segments.tr: O padrão não é "robôs substituem balconistas".

segments.src: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:
segments.tr: É que cada etapa da cadeia de varejo está ganhando um sensor e um loop de feedback:

segments.src: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.
segments.tr: - **Sensoriamento:** Tags RFID, câmeras de visão computacional e prateleiras inteligentes transformam "achamos que temos 40 unidades" em "sabemos que temos 37, e 3 estão no corredor errado". A precisão do estoque em vestuário historicamente flutuou bem abaixo de 100%, e fechar essa lacuna vale dinheiro real — você não pode vender o que seu sistema acha que está faltando.

segments.src: - **Deciding:** Machine-learning demand forecasting, automated replenishment, and algorithmic pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.
segments.tr: - **Decisão:** Previsão de demanda por aprendizado de máquina (machine learning), reposição automatizada e preços algorítmicos. As etiquetas eletrônicas de gôndola (ESLs) importam aqui não porque os preços mudam a cada hora (a maioria das redes os muda raramente, e fazê-lo agressivamente convida a reações negativas), mas porque o *custo de mudar um preço* cai para perto de zero. Quando uma decisão se torna barata, você a toma mais vezes.

segments.src: - **Selling:** Retail media networks — retailers selling ad space on their own sites, apps, and screens using their own purchase data. This is the most important business-model shift of the last decade. Amazon's advertising business alone runs in the tens of billions of dollars a year, and Walmart, Kroger, Target, and even gas-station chains now run their own. Why it matters: ad revenue carries far higher margins than selling groceries, so it can subsidize low prices. The retailer's real product starts to include *access to its shoppers*.
segments.tr: - **Venda:** Redes de mídia de varejo — varejistas vendendo espaço publicitário em seus próprios sites, aplicativos e telas usando seus próprios dados de compra. Esta é a mudança de modelo de negócios mais importante da última década. O negócio de publicidade da Amazon sozinho movimenta dezenas de bilhões de dólares por ano, e Walmart, Kroger, Target e até redes de postos de gasolina agora operam os seus próprios. Por que isso importa: a receita de publicidade traz margens muito maiores do que a venda de mantimentos, portanto pode subsidiar preços baixos. O verdadeiro produto do varejista começa a incluir o *acesso aos seus compradores*.

segments.src: - **Fulfilling:** Micro-fulfillment, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery. Note the honest part — these are expensive. Fulfilling a $40 online grocery order costs far more than letting a customer walk the aisles and do the picking for free.
segments.tr: - **Cumprimento (Fulfillment):** Micro-fulfillment, retirada na calçada (curbside pickup) e entrega no mesmo día. Note a parte honesta — estes são caros. Cumprir um pedido de supermercado online de $40 custa muito mais do que deixar um cliente caminhar pelos corredores e fazer a seleção de graça.

segments.src: Two cautionary notes, because hype is not analysis.
segments.tr: Duas notas de cautela, porque o hype não é análise.

segments.src: **Self-checkout** expanded fast, then several chains pulled it back or restricted it after shrink and customer-experience problems.
segments.tr: O **autoatendimento (self-checkout)** expandiu-se rapidamente, depois várias redes o retiraram ou restringiram após problemas de quebra (shrink) e experiência do cliente.

segments.src: **Fully autonomous "just walk out" stores** proved harder and costlier than early demos suggested; Amazon scaled back the format in its larger grocery stores.
segments.tr: Lojas **totalmente autônomas "just walk out" (basta sair)** provaram ser mais difíceis e custosas do que as primeiras demonstrações sugeriam; a Amazon reduziu o formato em suas lojas de supermercado maiores.

segments.src: The lesson from Lesson #2's *wheel of retailing* still holds: technology changes the cost curve, but it doesn't repeal the economics.
segments.tr: A lição da *roda do varejo* da Lição #2 ainda se mantém: a tecnologia muda a curva de custos, mas não revoga a economia.

segments.src: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**
segments.tr: Política de varejo — o livro de regras invisível.**

segments.src: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:
segments.tr: Os varejistas operam dentro de restrições estabelecidas por tribunais e legislaturas, e uma mudança de regra pode mover mais lucro do que qualquer decisão de merchandising:

segments.src: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.
segments.tr: - **Imposto sobre vendas:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) permitiu que os estados exijam que vendedores online de fora do estado coletem imposto sobre vendas. Isso acabou com uma vantagem de preço estrutural para o e-commerce da noite para o dia.

segments.src: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.
segments.tr: - **Responsabilidade de marketplaces:** A Lei INFORM Consumers (em vigor desde 2023) exige que os marketplaces online verifiquem vendedores terceirizados de alto volume — uma resposta ao crime organizado no varejo e a produtos falsificados.

segments.src: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.
segments.tr: - **Pagamentos:** As taxas de intercâmbio de cartões ("swipe fees") são um dos maiores itens de despesa de um varejista após mão de obra e aluguel, e têm sido objeto de anos de litígio e propostas legislativas repetidas.

segments.src: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.
segments.tr: - **Privacidade:** Leis estaduais lideradas pela CCPA/CPRA da Califórnia, além de mais de uma dezena de outras, restringem como os dados dos compradores por trás da mídia de varejo podem ser coletados e usados.

segments.src: - **Trade:** Tariffs and the treatment of low-value imported parcels (the "de minimis" exemption) have tightened in recent years — a reminder that one customs rule can reshape an entire business model, as it did for ultra-low-price direct-from-overseas apps.
segments.tr: - **Comércio:** Tarifas e o tratamento de encomendas importadas de baixo valor (a isenção "de minimis") endureceram nos últimos anos — um lembrete de que uma regra alfandegária pode remodelar todo um modelo de negócios, como fez para aplicativos de ultra-baixo preço direto do exterior.

segments.src: - **Labor and sustainability:** Minimum wage, scheduling laws, and packaging/extended-producer-responsibility rules all land directly on store P&Ls.
segments.tr: - **Trabalho e sustentabilidade:** Salário mínimo, leis de agendamento e regras de embalagem/responsabilidade estendida do produtor caem diretamente nos demonstrativos de resultados (P&Ls) das lojas.

segments.src: What actually stays constant.**
segments.tr: O que realmente permanece constante.**

segments.src: Strip away the tech and the same job remains: *get the right assortment, to the right place, at the right price, at an acceptable cost to serve.* Every trend above is a new way to do that old job — or a new constraint on doing it.
segments.tr: Elimine a tecnologia e o mesmo trabalho permanece: *obter o sortimento certo, no lugar certo, ao preço certo, a um custo aceitável para servir.* Cada tendência acima é uma nova maneira de fazer esse trabalho antigo — ou uma nova restrição para fazê-lo.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na Vida Quotidiana

segments.src: You're at a Target in Columbus, Ohio, buying a $12.99 bottle of laundry detergent.
segments.tr: Você está em um Target em Columbus, Ohio, comprando uma garrafa de $12,99 de sabão em pó.

segments.src: Trace what just touched that purchase.
segments.tr: Rastreie o que acabou de tocar nessa compra.

segments.src: You searched "detergent" in the app — the top result was a **sponsored placement** paid for by a brand through Target's retail media network.
segments.tr: Você pesquisou "detergent" no aplicativo — o principal resultado foi um **posicionamento patrocinado** pago por uma marca através da rede de mídia de varejo do Target.

segments.src: The app said the item was in Aisle D24 because an **inventory system** thinks that's where it is.
segments.tr: O aplicativo dizia que o item estava no Corredor D24 porque um **sistema de estoque** acha que é lá que ele está.

segments.src: The shelf price came from an **electronic label**, and it matched the app because unified pricing systems are table stakes now.
segments.tr: O preço na prateleira veio de uma **etiqueta eletrônica**, e coincidiu com o aplicativo porque sistemas de preços unificados são essenciais hoje em dia.

segments.src: You paid with a card; roughly 2–3% of that $12.99 left the retailer as an **interchange fee**.
segments.tr: Você pagou com cartão; aproximadamente 2–3% desses $12,99 saíram do varejista como uma **taxa de intercâmbio**.

segments.src: Sales tax was collected — and would have been collected identically if you'd ordered it online from an out-of-state seller, thanks to *Wayfair*.
segments.tr: O imposto sobre vendas foi cobrado — e teria sido cobrado de forma idêntica se você tivesse encomendado online de um vendedor de fora do estado, graças ao *Wayfair*.

segments.src: When you scanned out at self-checkout, a camera-based system was watching for scan avoidance.
segments.tr: Quando você passou pelo autoatendimento, um sistema baseado em câmera estava vigiando a evasão de escaneamento.

segments.src: Overnight, an **automated replenishment algorithm** will decide whether to reorder, and the data from your basket will help price the next brand's ad slot.
segments.tr: Durante a noite, um **algoritmo de reposição automatizada** decidirá se deve fazer um novo pedido, e os dados da sua cesta ajudarão a precificar o espaço de anúncio da próxima marca.

segments.src: One bottle of detergent.
segments.tr: Uma garrafa de sabão em pó.

segments.src: At least six of the technologies and policies above were involved, and you saw exactly none of them.
segments.tr: Pelo menos seis das tecnologias e políticas acima estavam envolvidas, e você não viu nenhuma delas.

segments.src: ## The Whole Series in Three Minutes
segments.tr: ## Toda a Série em Três Minutos

segments.src: - **#1–3 — Foundations:** Retailing is the last step of the distribution channel, where value is created through *sorting, breaking bulk, holding inventory, and providing service*. Formats (supermarket, warehouse club, specialty, off-price, e-commerce) evolve through the wheel of retailing: enter cheap and bare-bones, add service, drift upmarket, get undercut by the next entrant.
segments.tr: - **#1–3 — Fundamentos:** O varejo é o último passo do canal de distribuição, onde o valor é criado através da *seleção, fracionamento de volume, manutenção de estoque e prestação de serviços*. Os formatos (supermercado, clube de armazém, especialidade, off-price, e-commerce) evoluem através da roda do varejo: entram baratos e básicos, adicionam serviços, sobem de nível, são superados pelo próximo entrante.

segments.src: - **#4–6 — Customer and location:** Shopper decision-making, segmentation, and trade-area analysis. Location is retail's most expensive irreversible decision — you can change a price tomorrow, not a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: - **#4–6 — Cliente e localização:** Tomada de decisão do comprador, segmentação e análise de área de mercado. A localização é a decisão irreversível mais cara do varejo — você pode mudar um preço amanhã, não um contrato de arrendamento de 15 anos.

segments.src: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Assortment breadth vs. depth, category management, vendor negotiation, and pricing (cost-plus, competitive, psychological, markdown cadence, EDLP vs. high-low).
segments.tr: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Amplitude vs. profundidade de sortimento, gestão de categorias, negociação com fornecedores e preços (custo mais margem, competitivo, psicológico, cadência de markdown, EDLP vs. high-low).

segments.src: - **#10–12 — Operations:** Supply chain and inventory turnover, store layout and visual merchandising, promotion, loyalty, and CRM.
segments.tr: - **#10–12 — Operações:** Cadeia de suprimentos e giro de estoque, layout da loja e visual merchandising, promoção, fidelidade e CRM.

segments.src: - **#13–14 — Measurement and channels:** Retail's core metrics and the shift from multichannel to omnichannel to *unified commerce* — one inventory pool, one customer record, many touchpoints.
segments.tr: - **#13–14 — Medição e canais:** As principais métricas do varejo e a transição de multicanal para omnichannel e *comércio unificado* — um pool de estoque, um registro de cliente, muitos pontos de contato.

segments.src: The one formula worth remembering, in plain text:
segments.tr: A única fórmula que vale a pena lembrar, em texto simples:

segments.src: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost
segments.tr: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost

segments.src: It's the discipline of the whole field in one line: retail profit comes from **margin × velocity**, not margin alone.
segments.tr: É a disciplina de todo o campo em uma linha: o lucro do varejo vem de **margem × velocidade**, não apenas da margem.

segments.src: A high-margin item that never sells loses to a thin-margin item that turns twelve times a year.
segments.tr: Um item de alta margem que nunca vende perde para um item de margem fina que gira doze vezes por ano.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo de Três Linhas

segments.src: 1. Retail's frontier is instrumentation — sensing, deciding, selling, and fulfilling are all becoming data loops, with retail media networks the single biggest business-model change.
segments.tr: 1. A fronteira do varejo é a instrumentação — sensoriamento, decisão, venda e cumprimento estão se tornando loops de dados, sendo as redes de mídia de varejo a maior mudança individual de modelo de negócios.

segments.src: 2. Policy is not background noise: sales tax nexus, marketplace verification, interchange fees, privacy law, and trade rules each move real money.
segments.tr: 2. A política não é ruído de fundo: o nexo de imposto sobre vendas, verificação de marketplace, taxas de intercâmbio, lei de privacidade e regras comerciais movimentam dinheiro real cada.

segments.src: 3. Underneath it all, the job hasn't changed — right assortment, right place, right price, acceptable cost to serve — and GMROI is still how you know you're doing it.
segments.tr: 3. Por trás de tudo isso, o trabalho não mudou — sortimento certo, lugar certo, preço certo, custo aceitável para servir — e o GMROI ainda é como você sabe que está fazendo isso certo.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Retail media network** — A retailer's own advertising business, selling placements on its site, app, and in-store screens using its first-party purchase data.
segments.tr: - **Rede de mídia de varejo (Retail media network)** — O próprio negócio de publicidade de um varejista, vendendo espaços em seu site, aplicativo e telas nas lojas usando seus dados de compra primários.

segments.src: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — A digital price display on the shelf edge, updated centrally; its value is driving the cost of a price change toward zero.
segments.tr: - **Etiqueta eletrônica de gôndola (ESL)** — Um display de preço digital na borda da prateleira, atualizado centralmente; seu valor é impulsionar o custo de uma mudança de preço em direção a zero.

segments.src: - **Unified commerce** — A single shared inventory, pricing, and customer record behind every channel, as opposed to separate online and store systems stitched together.
segments.tr: - **Comércio unificado** — Um único estoque compartilhado, preços e registro de cliente por trás de cada canal, em oposição a sistemas separados online e de loja unidos.

segments.src: - **Economic nexus** — The rule, established for sales tax by *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, that a seller can owe tax collection duties in a state based on sales volume there, without a physical location.
segments.tr: - **Nexo econômico** — A regra, estabelecida para imposto sobre vendas por *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, de que um vendedor pode dever obrigações de cobrança de impostos em um estado com base no volume de vendas lá, sem uma localização física.

segments.src: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Gross margin dollars per dollar of inventory carried; retail's core test of whether margin and turnover are working together.
segments.tr: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Dólares de margem bruta por dólar de estoque mantido; o teste principal do varejo sobre se a margem e o giro estão trabalhando juntos.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** A retail media network is the retailer monetizing its own audience and purchase data; the high margins on that ad revenue can subsidize lower shelf prices.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** Frequent demand-based price hikes invite consumer and political backlash, and most chains avoid them.

segments.tr: O verdadeiro valor é operacional: custo quase zero por mudança de preço, além de consistência de preço entre prateleira e aplicativo e menos trabalho gasto com etiquetas de papel.

in.title: [Retailing 101 #15] Toko Menjadi Perangkat Lunak — dan Seluruh Semester Anda dalam Satu Halaman

segments.src: > Retail's next decade is being written by two forces most shoppers never see — technology that turns the store into a data system, and policy that quietly sets the rules of the shelf. Here's where the industry is heading, plus a one-page recap of everything this series covered.
segments.tr: > Dekade berikutnya dalam dunia ritel dibentuk oleh dua kekuatan yang jarang dilihat oleh sebagian besar pembelanja — teknologi yang mengubah toko menjadi sistem data, dan kebijakan yang secara diam-diam menetapkan aturan di rak. segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: For most of its history, retail was a **physical** business that happened to keep records.
segments.tr: Sebagian besar sejarah ritel adalah bisnis **fisik** yang kebetulan menyimpan catatan.

segments.src: Today it's an **information** business that happens to have buildings.
segments.tr: Hari ini, ritel adalah bisnis **informasi** yang kebetulan memiliki bangunan.

segments.src: That single inversion explains almost every trend on the horizon.
segments.tr: Pembalikan tunggal itu menjelaskan hampir setiap tren yang sedang berkembang.

segments.src: Break it into three layers.
segments.tr: Mari kita bagi menjadi tiga lapisan.

segments.src: Retail tech ("retailtech") — the store becomes instrumented.**
segments.tr: Teknologi ritel ("retailtech") — toko dilengkapi dengan instrumen.**

segments.src: The pattern isn't "robots replace clerks."
segments.tr: Polanya bukanlah "robot menggantikan kasir."

segments.src: It's that every step in the retail chain is getting a sensor and a feedback loop:
segments.tr: Melainkan setiap langkah dalam rantai ritel mendapatkan sensor dan siklus umpan balik:

segments.src: - **Sensing:** RFID tags, computer-vision cameras, and smart shelves turn "we think we have 40 units" into "we know we have 37, and 3 are in the wrong aisle." Inventory accuracy in apparel has historically hovered well below 100%, and closing that gap is worth real money — you can't sell what your system thinks is missing.
segments.tr: - **Penginderaan:** Label RFID, kamera visi komputer, dan rak pintar mengubah "kami pikir kami punya 40 unit" menjadi "kami tahu kami punya 37, dan 3 ada di lorong yang salah." Keakuratan inventaris dalam pakaian secara historis berada jauh di bawah 100%, dan menutup kesenjangan itu bernilai uang nyata — Anda tidak dapat menjual apa yang oleh sistem Anda dianggap hilang.

segments.src: - **Deciding:** Machine-learning demand forecasting, automated replenishment, and algorithmic pricing. Electronic shelf labels (ESLs) matter here not because prices change hourly (most chains change them rarely, and doing so aggressively invites backlash), but because the *cost of changing a price* drops to near zero. When a decision gets cheap, you make it more often.
segments.tr: - **Pengambilan Keputusan:** Peramalan permintaan pembelajaran mesin, pengisian ulang otomatis, dan penetapan harga algoritmik. Label harga elektronik (ESL) penting di sini bukan karena harga berubah setiap jam (sebagian besar jaringan jarang mengubahnya, dan melakukannya secara agresif mengundang reaksi keras), tetapi karena *biaya mengubah harga* turun mendekati nol. Ketika sebuah keputusan menjadi murah, Anda akan lebih sering melakukannya.

segments.src: - **Selling:** Retail media networks — retailers selling ad space on their own sites, apps, and screens using their own purchase data. This is the most important business-model shift of the last decade. Amazon's advertising business alone runs in the tens of billions of dollars a year, and Walmart, Kroger, Target, and even gas-station chains now run their own. Why it matters: ad revenue carries far higher margins than selling groceries, so it can subsidize low prices. The retailer's real product starts to include *access to its shoppers*.
segments.tr: - **Penjualan:** Jaringan media ritel — peritel menjual ruang iklan di situs, aplikasi, dan layar mereka sendiri menggunakan data pembelian mereka sendiri. Ini adalah pergeseran model bisnis paling penting dalam dekade terakhir. Bisnis periklanan Amazon sendiri mencapai puluhan miliar dolar setahun, dan Walmart, Kroger, Target, bahkan jaringan SPBU kini menjalankan bisnis mereka sendiri. Mengapa ini penting: pendapatan iklan menghasilkan margin yang jauh lebih tinggi daripada menjual bahan makanan, sehingga dapat mensubsidi harga murah. Produk nyata peritel mulai mencakup *akses ke pembelinya*.

segments.src: - **Fulfilling:** Micro-fulfillment, curbside pickup, and same-day delivery. Note the honest part — these are expensive. Fulfilling a $40 online grocery order costs far more than letting a customer walk the aisles and do the picking for free.
segments.tr: - **Pemenuhan Pesanan:** Pemenuhan mikro, pengambilan di tepi jalan, dan pengiriman di hari yang sama. Perhatikan bagian yang jujur — hal-hal ini mahal. Memenuhi pesanan bahan makanan online senilai $40 jauh lebih mahal daripada membiarkan pelanggan berjalan di lorong dan melakukan pengambilan sendiri secara gratis.

segments.src: Two cautionary notes, because hype is not analysis.
segments.tr: Dua catatan peringatan, karena sensasi bukanlah analisis.

segments.src: **Self-checkout** expanded fast, then several chains pulled it back or restricted it after shrink and customer-experience problems.
segments.tr: **Kasir mandiri** berkembang pesat, kemudian beberapa jaringan menariknya kembali atau membatasinya setelah masalah penyusutan dan pengalaman pelanggan.

segments.src: **Fully autonomous "just walk out" stores** proved harder and costlier than early demos suggested; Amazon scaled back the format in its larger grocery stores.
segments.tr: **Toko otonom penuh "just walk out"** terbukti lebih sulit dan lebih mahal daripada yang disarankan oleh demo awal; Amazon mengurangi format tersebut di toko kelontongnya yang lebih besar.

segments.src: The lesson from Lesson #2's *wheel of retailing* still holds: technology changes the cost curve, but it doesn't repeal the economics.
segments.tr: Pelajaran dari *wheel of retailing* Pelajaran #2 tetap berlaku: teknologi mengubah kurva biaya, tetapi tidak mencabut ilmu ekonomi.

segments.src: Retail policy — the invisible rulebook.**
segments.tr: Kebijakan ritel — buku aturan yang tak kasat mata.**

segments.src: Retailers operate inside constraints set by courts and legislatures, and a rule change can move more profit than any merchandising decision:
segments.tr: Peritel beroperasi di dalam batasan yang ditetapkan oleh pengadilan dan badan legislatif, dan perubahan aturan dapat menggerakkan lebih banyak keuntungan daripada keputusan merchandising apa pun:

segments.src: - **Sales tax:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) let states require out-of-state online sellers to collect sales tax. It ended a structural price advantage for e-commerce overnight.
segments.tr: - **Pajak Penjualan:** *South Dakota v. Wayfair* (2018) mengizinkan negara bagian mewajibkan penjual online luar negara bagian untuk memungut pajak penjualan. Ini mengakhiri keunggulan harga struktural untuk e-commerce dalam semalam.

segments.src: - **Marketplace accountability:** The INFORM Consumers Act (in force since 2023) requires online marketplaces to verify high-volume third-party sellers — a response to organized retail crime and counterfeit goods.
segments.tr: - **Akuntabilitas Pasar:** INFORM Consumers Act (berlaku sejak 2023) mewajibkan pasar online untuk memverifikasi penjual pihak ketiga bervolume tinggi — sebagai respons terhadap kejahatan ritel terorganisir dan barang palsu.

segments.src: - **Payments:** Card interchange ("swipe") fees are one of a retailer's largest line items after labor and rent, and they've been the subject of years of litigation and repeated legislative proposals.
segments.tr: - **Pembayaran:** Biaya pertukaran kartu ("gesek") adalah salah satu pos pengeluaran terbesar peritel setelah tenaga kerja dan sewa, dan telah menjadi subjek litigasi bertahun-tahun serta proposal legislatif berulang.

segments.src: - **Privacy:** State laws led by California's CCPA/CPRA, plus more than a dozen others, constrain how the shopper data behind retail media can be collected and used.
segments.tr: - **Privasi:** Undang-undang negara bagian yang dipimpin oleh CCPA/CPRA California, ditambah lebih dari selusin undang-undang lainnya, membatasi bagaimana data pembelanja di balik media ritel dapat dikumpulkan dan digunakan.

segments.src: - **Trade:** Tariffs and the treatment of low-value imported parcels (the "de minimis" exemption) have tightened in recent years — a reminder that one customs rule can reshape an entire business model, as it did for ultra-low-price direct-from-overseas apps.
segments.tr: - **Perdagangan:** Tarif dan perlakuan terhadap paket impor bernilai rendah (pengecualian "de minimis") telah diperketat dalam beberapa tahun terakhir — sebuah pengingat bahwa satu aturan pabean dapat merubah seluruh model bisnis, seperti yang terjadi pada aplikasi langsung dari luar negeri berharga sangat murah.

segments.src: - **Labor and sustainability:** Minimum wage, scheduling laws, and packaging/extended-producer-responsibility rules all land directly on store P&Ls.
segments.tr: - **Tenaga kerja dan keberlanjutan:** Upah minimum, undang-undang penjadwalan, dan aturan pengemasan/tanggung jawab produsen yang diperluas semuanya berdampak langsung pada laba rugi toko.

segments.src: What actually stays constant.**
segments.tr: Apa yang benar-benar tetap konstan.**

segments.src: Strip away the tech and the same job remains: *get the right assortment, to the right place, at the right price, at an acceptable cost to serve.* Every trend above is a new way to do that old job — or a new constraint on doing it.
segments.tr: Singkirkan teknologinya dan pekerjaan yang sama tetap ada: *dapatkan jenis yang tepat, ke tempat yang tepat, dengan harga yang tepat, dengan biaya layanan yang dapat diterima.* Setiap tren di atas adalah cara baru untuk melakukan pekerjaan lama tersebut — atau batasan baru dalam melakukannya.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: You're at a Target in Columbus, Ohio, buying a $12.99 bottle of laundry detergent.
segments.tr: Anda berada di Target di Columbus, Ohio, membeli sebotol deterjen cucian seharga $12.99.

segments.src: Trace what just touched that purchase.
segments.tr: Lacak apa saja yang baru saja menyentuh pembelian tersebut.

segments.src: You searched "detergent" in the app — the top result was a **sponsored placement** paid for by a brand through Target's retail media network.
segments.tr: Anda mencari "deterjen" di aplikasi — hasil teratas adalah **penempatan bersponsor** yang dibayar oleh sebuah merek melalui jaringan media ritel Target.

segments.src: The app said the item was in Aisle D24 because an **inventory system** thinks that's where it is.
segments.tr: Aplikasi tersebut mengatakan barang itu berada di Lorong D24 karena **sistem inventaris** mengira di itulah tempatnya.

segments.src: The shelf price came from an **electronic label**, and it matched the app because unified pricing systems are table stakes now.
segments.tr: Harga di rak berasal dari **label elektronik**, dan itu cocok dengan aplikasi karena sistem penetapan harga yang disatukan adalah hal yang mutlak sekarang.

segments.src: You paid with a card; roughly 2–3% of that $12.99 left the retailer as an **interchange fee**.
segments.tr: Anda membayar dengan kartu; sekitar 2–3% dari $12.99 tersebut meninggalkan peritel sebagai **biaya pertukaran**.

segments.src: Sales tax was collected — and would have been collected identically if you'd ordered it online from an out-of-state seller, thanks to *Wayfair*.
segments.tr: Pajak penjualan dipungut — dan akan dipungut secara identik jika Anda memesannya secara online dari penjual luar negara bagian, berkat *Wayfair*.

segments.src: When you scanned out at self-checkout, a camera-based system was watching for scan avoidance.
segments.tr: Saat Anda memindai keluar di kasir mandiri, sistem berbasis kamera mengawasi penghindaran pemindaian.

segments.src: Overnight, an **automated replenishment algorithm** will decide whether to reorder, and the data from your basket will help price the next brand's ad slot.
segments.tr: Semalam, **algoritma pengisian ulang otomatis** akan memutuskan apakah akan memesan ulang, dan data dari keranjang Anda akan membantu menentukan harga slot iklan merek berikutnya.

segments.src: One bottle of detergent.
segments.tr: Satu botol deterjen.

segments.src: At least six of the technologies and policies above were involved, and you saw exactly none of them.
segments.tr: Setidaknya enam dari teknologi dan kebijakan di atas terlibat, dan Anda tidak melihat satupun dari mereka.

segments.src: ## The Whole Series in Three Minutes
segments.tr: ## Seluruh Seri dalam Tiga Menit

segments.src: - **#1–3 — Foundations:** Retailing is the last step of the distribution channel, where value is created through *sorting, breaking bulk, holding inventory, and providing service*. Formats (supermarket, warehouse club, specialty, off-price, e-commerce) evolve through the wheel of retailing: enter cheap and bare-bones, add service, drift upmarket, get undercut by the next entrant.
segments.tr: - **#1–3 — Landasan:** Ritel adalah langkah terakhir dari saluran distribusi, di mana nilai diciptakan melalui *penyortiran, pemecahan jumlah besar, penyimpanan inventaris, dan penyediaan layanan*. Format (supermarket, klub gudang, khusus, diskon, e-commerce) berkembang melalui roda ritel: masuk dengan murah dan sederhana, menambahkan layanan, naik kelas, dikalahkan oleh pendatang berikutnya.

segments.src: - **#4–6 — Customer and location:** Shopper decision-making, segmentation, and trade-area analysis. Location is retail's most expensive irreversible decision — you can change a price tomorrow, not a 15-year lease.
segments.tr: - **#4–6 — Pelanggan dan lokasi:** Pengambilan keputusan pembelanja, segmentasi, and analisis area perdagangan. Lokasi adalah keputusan mahal yang tidak dapat diubah dalam ritel — Anda dapat mengubah harga besok, bukan sewa 15 tahun.

segments.src: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Assortment breadth vs. depth, category management, vendor negotiation, and pricing (cost-plus, competitive, psychological, markdown cadence, EDLP vs. high-low).
segments.tr: - **#7–9 — Merchandising:** Luas vs kedalaman ragam produk, manajemen kategori, negosiasi vendor, dan penetapan harga (biaya plus, kompetitif, psikologis, irama penurunan harga, EDLP vs tinggi-rendah).

segments.src: - **#10–12 — Operations:** Supply chain and inventory turnover, store layout and visual merchandising, promotion, loyalty, and CRM.
segments.tr: - **#10–12 — Operasi:** Rantai pasokan dan perputaran inventaris, tata letak toko dan merchandising visual, promosi, loyalitas, dan CRM.

segments.src: - **#13–14 — Measurement and channels:** Retail's core metrics and the shift from multichannel to omnichannel to *unified commerce* — one inventory pool, one customer record, many touchpoints.
segments.tr: - **#13–14 — Pengukuran dan saluran:** Metrik inti ritel dan pergeseran dari multisaluran ke omnichannel ke *perdagangan terpadu* — satu kumpulan inventaris, satu catatan pelanggan, banyak titik sentuh.

segments.src: The one formula worth remembering, in plain text:
segments.tr: Satu rumus yang perlu diingat, dalam teks biasa:

segments.src: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost
segments.tr: GMROI = Gross Margin $ / Average Inventory Cost

segments.src: It's the discipline of the whole field in one line: retail profit comes from **margin × velocity**, not margin alone.
segments.tr: Ini adalah disiplin seluruh bidang dalam satu baris: keuntungan ritel berasal dari **margin × kecepatan**, bukan margin saja.

segments.src: A high-margin item that never sells loses to a thin-margin item that turns twelve times a year.
segments.tr: Barang dengan margin tinggi yang tidak pernah terjual kalah dengan barang ber margin tipis yang berputar dua belas kali setahun.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Retail's frontier is instrumentation — sensing, deciding, selling, and fulfilling are all becoming data loops, with retail media networks the single biggest business-model change.
segments.tr: 1. Perbatasan ritel adalah instrumentasi — penginderaan, pengambilan keputusan, penjualan, dan pemenuhan semuanya menjadi siklus data, dengan jaringan media ritel sebagai perubahan model bisnis terbesar.

segments.src: 2. Policy is not background noise: sales tax nexus, marketplace verification, interchange fees, privacy law, and trade rules each move real money.
segments.tr: 2. Kebijakan bukanlah kebisingan latar belakang: hubungan pajak penjualan, verifikasi pasar, biaya pertukaran, undang-undang privasi, and aturan perdagangan masing-masing menggerakkan uang nyata.

segments.src: 3. Underneath it all, the job hasn't changed — right assortment, right place, right price, acceptable cost to serve — and GMROI is still how you know you're doing it.
segments.tr: 3. Di balik semua itu, pekerjaan tidak berubah — jenis yang tepat, tempat yang tepat, harga yang tepat, biaya layanan yang dapat diterima — dan GMROI masih menjadi cara untuk mengetahui bahwa Anda melakukannya dengan benar.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Retail media network** — A retailer's own advertising business, selling placements on its site, app, and in-store screens using its first-party purchase data.
segments.tr: - **Retail media network** — Bisnis periklanan milik peritel sendiri, menjual penempatan di situs, aplikasi, dan layar di dalam toko menggunakan data pembelian pihak pertama mereka.

segments.src: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — A digital price display on the shelf edge, updated centrally; its value is driving the cost of a price change toward zero.
segments.tr: - **Electronic shelf label (ESL)** — Tampilan harga digital di tepi rak, diperbarui secara terpusat; nilainya adalah mendorong biaya perubahan harga mendekati nol.

segments.src: - **Unified commerce** — A single shared inventory, pricing, and customer record behind every channel, as opposed to separate online and store systems stitched together.
segments.tr: - **Unified commerce** — Inventaris, penetapan harga, dan catatan pelanggan bersama tunggal di balik setiap saluran, alih-alih sistem online dan toko terpisah yang disatukan.

segments.src: - **Economic nexus** — The rule, established for sales tax by *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, that a seller can owe tax collection duties in a state based on sales volume there, without a physical location.
segments.tr: - **Economic nexus** — Aturan, yang ditetapkan untuk pajak penjualan oleh *South Dakota v. Wayfair*, bahwa seorang penjual dapat memiliki kewajiban pemungutan pajak di suatu negara bagian berdasarkan volume penjualan di sana, tanpa lokasi fisik.

segments.src: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Gross margin dollars per dollar of inventory carried; retail's core test of whether margin and turnover are working together.
segments.tr: - **GMROI (Gross Margin Return on Inventory Investment)** — Dolar margin kotor per dolar inventaris yang dibawa; uji inti ritel apakah margin and perputaran bekerja sama.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** A retail media network is the retailer monetizing its own audience and purchase data; the high margins on that ad revenue can subsidize lower shelf prices.
segments.tr: *Jawaban: **Q1 — B.** Jaringan media ritel adalah peritel yang memonetisasi audiens dan data pembelinya sendiri; margin tinggi pada pendapatan iklan tersebut dapat mensubsidi harga rak yang lebih rendah.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (False).** Frequent demand-based price hikes invite consumer and political backlash, and most chains avoid them.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (Salah).** Kenaikan harga berbasis permintaan yang sering mengundang reaksi konsumen dan politik, dan sebagian besar jaringan menghindarinya.

segments.src: The real value is operational: near-zero cost per price change, plus shelf-to-app price consistency and less labor spent on paper tags.
segments.tr: Nilai sebenarnya adalah operasional: biaya mendekati nol per perubahan harga, ditambah konsistensi harga rak-ke-aplikasi dan lebih sedikit tenaga kerja yang dihabiskan untuk label kertas.

segments.src: **Q3 — C.** Before Wayfair, many remote online sellers weren't required to collect state sales tax, effectively making their prices several percent cheaper than a local store's.
segments.tr: **Q3 — C.** Sebelum Wayfair, banyak penjual online jarak jauh tidak diwajibkan memungut pajak penjualan negara bagian, secara efektif membuat harga mereka beberapa persen lebih murah daripada toko lokal.

segments.src: The 2018 decision ended that gap.
segments.tr: Keputusan 2018 mengakhiri kesenjangan tersebut.
